structure.title: Preface
structure.summary: This letter from Axis Bank to stock exchanges informs about the 31st Annual General Meeting (AGM) and Integrated Annual Report for fiscal 2025, referencing SEBI regulations. It encloses the AGM Notice and Annual Report, provides website access, and details the businesses to be transacted. These include ordinary business: adoption of standalone and consolidated financial statements, dividend declaration, and re-appointment of director Mini Ipe. Special business covers appointment of secretarial auditors, revisions in remuneration for MD & CEO Amitabh Chaudhry and Executive Directors Subrat Mohanty and Munish Sharda, enhancement of borrowing limit to Rs. 3,00,000 crores, raising funds via debt securities up to Rs. 35,000 crores and equity shares up to Rs. 20,000 crores, and material related party transactions with LIC, LIC Housing Finance, IDBI Bank, and Axis Max Life Insurance.

Special business includes appointment of M/s. Bhandari & Associates as Secretarial Auditors for five years, revision in remuneration of MD & CEO Amitabh Chaudhry and Executive Directors Subrat Mohanty and Munish Sharda effective 1 April 2025, enhancement of borrowing limit to Rs. 3,00,000 crores, raising funds via debt securities up to Rs. 35,000 crores and equity shares up to Rs. 20,000 crores, and material related party transactions with Life Insurance Corporation of India, LIC Housing Finance Limited, IDBI Bank Limited, and Axis Max Life Insurance Limited. The notice also details resolution types and legal provisions.

nodes.title: Integrated Business Lines
nodes.summary:
Integrated Business Lines
Axis Bank’s integrated business lines offer a comprehensive suite of customised financial solutions to individuals, businesses, and institutions across India. This unified approach leverages digital innovation, domain expertise, and a strong physical presence to holistically serve customers through every stage of their financial journey.

nodes.title: Retail Banking
nodes.summary: This text covers three banking segments: Retail Banking, Wholesale and Commercial Banking, and integrated business lines through 'One Axis'. Retail Banking details personalized solutions for individuals, small businesses, and Bharat Banking customers via digital and physical networks, listing products like deposits, cards, loans, payments, forex, wealth management, and third-party distribution, with Y-o-Y performance highlights for retail term deposits, retail loan book, and Burgundy Private AUM. Wholesale and Commercial Banking serves Indian corporates and MSMEs with relationship-led customized solutions, listing products such as corporate and SME loans, deposits, payments, trade finance, forex, derivatives, cash management, and commercial cards, with Y-o-Y highlights for corporate, mid-corporate, and SME loans. 'One Axis' integrates offerings across segments and subsidiaries, listing investments, broking, asset management, insurance, invoice discounting, trustee services, and payments, with performance highlights including total subsidiary investment, combined net worth, and combined PAT.

nodes.title: Wholesale, Commercial Banking and One Axis Offerings
nodes.summary: The page covers Wholesale and Commercial Banking, detailing how the bank serves Indian corporates and MSMEs through a relationship-led model with digital innovation. It lists products and services including corporate and SME loans, term deposits, payments, trade finance, letters of credit, guarantees, foreign exchange, derivatives, cash management, and commercial cards. Year-on-year performance highlights show 8% growth in corporate loans, 10% in mid-corporate loan book, and 14% in SME loan book. It also covers offerings through 'One Axis,' an integrated approach combining business segments and subsidiaries to deliver holistic financial solutions. Products include investments and broking, asset management and insurance, an MSME digital invoice discounting platform, trustee services, and payments. Performance highlights show ₹3,812 crores total investment in subsidiaries as of March 31, 2025.

nodes.title: Promoting enduring value for our stakeholders
nodes.summary: Axis Bank's Integrated Annual Report 2024–25 highlights steady progress and transformation under sound governance. It covers global economic uncertainty due to U.S. trade shifts and tariffs, India's moderated growth with prudent fiscal and monetary policies, and the Bank's strong financial performance including RoA of 1.77%, RoE of 16.89%, and robust asset quality. It discusses customer obsession program Sparsh 2.0, top-tier corporate governance rating, ESG initiatives with a standalone Board-level committee and sustainable lending targets, and CSR efforts through Axis Bank Foundation's Mission 2 Million. It also acknowledges retiring Deputy Managing Director Rajiv Anand.

nodes.title: Anchored to a sound strategic framework
nodes.summary: The text outlines a strategic framework anchored in customer centricity and digital excellence, comprising six pillars. S1 'One Axis' ecosystem integrates products for tailored solutions. S2 digital-first banking with innovations like 'open' and 'neo', multilingual and WhatsApp banking. S3 Bharat Banking empowers rural India via financial inclusion. S4 nation-building through government partnerships for public finance, infrastructure, and service delivery. S5 stakeholder value creation for customers, employees, investors, and communities. S6 environmental sustainability with green practices, Mission 2 Million trees upgraded to 8 million by 2030, and ESG goals.

nodes.title: Our action plan for a greener tomorrow
nodes.summary: Axis Bank outlines its ESG strategy, anchored in governance and stakeholder priorities, with material issues and SDG linkages. It details its climate action plan focused on reducing risk, enabling green growth, and building resilience, aligned with UN SDGs and India's NDCs. Key commitments include sustainable financing, inclusive banking, and climate-aligned products, overseen by the Board's ESG Committee. The plan addresses portfolio risk assessment, climate stress testing, carbon footprint reduction, CSR initiatives, and lending shifts. Specific targets cover incremental financing for positive-impact sectors, EV portfolio percentages, reducing carbon-intensive exposure, women's workforce representation, and tree planting, with progress reported for March 2023, 2024, and 2025.

nodes.title: Facilitating banking, anytime, anywhere
nodes.summary: The text details the bank's extensive physical and digital reach, including 5,879 domestic branches, 13,941 ATMs, and international offices, serving individuals, MSMEs, farmers, corporates, and entrepreneurs through customized solutions. It highlights strategic expansion in rural and semi-urban areas with specialized branches like Platinum and RuSu, and inclusive infrastructure. Digital banking features a mobile app with ~3 crore customers, 250+ DIY services, high app ratings, and significant transaction volumes. Phygital engagement includes 8 virtual centers, 1,700 virtual relationship managers, ~106 million Aha! conversations, and WhatsApp banking with 30 million users, 40 digitized product journeys, and ₹191 crores in fixed deposits booked.

nodes.title: Branch Profile and Digital Banking Overview
nodes.summary: The page covers Branch Profile and Digital Banking. Branch Profile includes region-wise distribution (Metro 30%, Urban 23%, Semi-urban 29%, Rural 18%) and geography-wise distribution (North 23%, South 33%, East 21%, West 23%), along with branch types: RuSu branches (asset-light for rural India), Platinum branches (for Small Banking Business customers), and inclusive infrastructure for older people, women, and customers with disabilities. Digital Banking highlights a real-time, seamless, secure ecosystem with investments in technology, offering end-to-end solutions. Key metrics: ~3 crores mobile banking registered customers, ~15 million non-Axis customers using Axis Mobile & Axis Pay, 250+ DIY services, 71% mobile-only banking customers, app ratings 4.8 (Apple) and 4.7 (Google Play), ₹25.7 trillion mobile banking spends (20% y-o-y), and 8.7 billion transactions (36% y-o-y).

nodes.title: Moments that shaped our journey
nodes.summary: This text chronicles Axis Bank's evolution from its 1994 founding as UTI Bank under 1993 RBI guidelines to becoming a major private bank, emphasizing resilience and innovation. It details 1990s milestones like the first branch, deposits crossing ₹1,000 crores, and an oversubscribed IPO. The 2000s cover branch expansion, rebranding to Axis Bank, corporate internet banking, ATM network growth, and London Stock Exchange listing. The 2010s highlight leadership appointments, acquisitions of Enam Securities and Citibank India's consumer business, online trading launch, green bonds, and GIFT City IFSC unit. The 2020s section covers a large QIP, Max Life partnership, LGBTQIA+ inclusivity charter, ESG-compliant Sustainable AT1 Bond, and 2024-25 achievements including the 5,000th branch and Citibank customer migration.

nodes.title: A resilient foundation laid with trust

It describes subsidiaries as strategic levers offering services in lending, wealth management, investments, insurance, and digital distribution. The 'One Axis' approach integrates customer experience across the financial lifecycle through collaboration and bundled solutions. It provides paid-up equity share capital of ₹619.47 crores as of March 31, 2025, and includes a shareholding pattern with percentages for Foreign Institutional Investors (7.91%), Life Insurance Corporation of India (42.48%), Indian Institutions (39.52%), GDRs (6.76%), and Others (3.33%).

nodes.title: ‘One Axis’ Ecosystem
nodes.summary: The 'One Axis' ecosystem highlights strategic synergies from the Bank's universal banking model, offering diversified financial solutions across customer segments. It emphasizes cross-selling through 5,000+ branches and digital channels, API integrations, common CRM platforms, and integrated offerings in investments, protection, lending, and advisory, focusing on profitability and customer stickiness. It lists key subsidiaries and associates with ownership percentages and core business segments, including Axis Finance, Axis Securities, Axis Capital, Axis Asset Management, Axis Trustee Services, Axis Max Life Insurance, Axis Pension Fund Management, Freecharge, and A.TReDS. Fiscal 2025 highlights include PAT figures, AUM growth, and GMV increases, along with market positioning statements for each entity.

nodes.title: Staying ahead in a dynamically evolving environment
nodes.summary: The text discusses the Bank's strategic positioning in a dynamic environment, covering global and Indian economic outlooks, regulatory changes, and competitive advantages. It highlights global challenges like inflation and trade tensions, while India's GDP growth is projected at 6.5%. The regulatory landscape shifts toward risk sensitivity, digital integrity, and sustainability, with RBI and SEBI tightening norms. The Bank's strategy includes diversification, digital penetration, and the 'One Axis' ecosystem. Key trends reshaping Indian banking are outlined: formal credit expansion, deposit pressure, regulatory tightening, digital-first behavior, climate integration, and AI/embedded finance. The Bank's responses include granular deposit growth, compliance-by-design, GenAI tools, ESG initiatives, and API-led ecosystems. Finally, competitive metrics as of March 31, 2025, are presented, showing total assets, advances, CASA ratio, NIM, net NPA, ROE, credit card market share, UPI payer share, and POS acquiring rank, with commentary on its position as the 3rd largest private bank.

nodes.title: What Differentiates Us
nodes.summary: The text outlines Axis Bank's competitive differentiators: blending scale with service, technology with trust, and strategy with social consciousness. It highlights ecosystem partnerships with Flipkart, Airtel, Indian Oil, and CSCs to embed banking in daily life. Financial inclusion via RuSu strategy with 2,736 Bharat Banking branches, 28,000+ CSC entrepreneurs, and Business Correspondents is detailed. Digital intelligence includes GenAI tools 'Adi' and 'neo', and digital transaction adoption. A risk-aware approach emphasizes governance, Board-level risk oversight, and compliance. The 'One Axis' model offers full-spectrum financial services through subsidiaries. Marketing initiatives include the 'Har raah dil se open' campaign celebrating 100,000 employees, the #AchhaiKabhiRukniNahiChahiye festive campaign, and ACHH.AI, a GenAI platform for curated offers and sustainable gifting.

nodes.title: Engaging with purpose and addressing what matters
nodes.summary: Axis Bank emphasizes purposeful stakeholder engagement to understand expectations, assess business environment and material issues, and shape strategy for long-term value. It conducts periodic Stakeholder Engagement and Materiality Assessment (SEMA) with internal and external stakeholders, including a fiscal 2025 Double Materiality Assessment aligned with CSRD. The process involves stakeholder identification, categorization, prioritization, IRO identification, and materiality matrix development. Eight key stakeholder groups were identified and prioritized via a matrix. For investors, the text details why they matter, communication channels, frequency, shared value creation, key concerns, and responses anchored in the GPS strategy, highlighting financial performance, governance, ESG, and sustainable value creation.

nodes.title: Investors
nodes.summary: The text details how a bank creates value for investors, emphasizing their role as capital providers and the importance of transparent communication. It outlines engagement methods (earnings calls, conferences, roadshows, meetings), frequency (continuous/periodic/need-based), and investor priorities including financial performance, governance, strategy, ESG, responsible banking, and technology. The bank's response via its GPS strategy includes sustainable growth, ethical governance, responsible banking, agility, risk management, and stakeholder dialogue. Value delivery is demonstrated through financial performance, EPS growth, asset quality, capital position, low NPAs, ESG ratings, CSR initiatives, customer satisfaction (NPS), and digital innovation, integrating profitability, responsibility, and governance for long-term stakeholder value.

nodes.title: Customers
nodes.summary: This text outlines the importance of customers to the bank, emphasizing that helping them reach financial goals through diverse products and services directly impacts their financial health and shared success. It details communication channels including branches, relationship managers, online platforms, virtual centre, surveys, grievance mechanisms, and marketing campaigns, with continuous or need-based frequency. Key customer priorities include quality products, innovative technology, transparency, data privacy, and effective grievance redressal. The bank responds with a 'One Axis' approach, customized products, ethical practices, digitization, the Axis Pride grievance resolution initiative, sustainable financing, regular surveys, and leadership in digital banking. Shared value creation is reflected in a Retail NPS of 159, 59 million customers as of March 31, 2025, an extensive branch and ATM network, accessibility features for persons with disabilities (Braille keypads, voice guidance, ramps), and doorstep banking for senior citizens and PWDs.

nodes.title: Regulators & Policymakers
nodes.summary: This text outlines the engagement with regulators and policymakers as stakeholders. It explains why they matter, detailing how stringent fiduciary and regulatory standards, capital requirements, lending practices, financial reporting, priority sector lending targets, and cybersecurity policies impact banks' strategy and profitability. It covers how Axis Bank connects with them through mandatory filings, inspections, meetings, email correspondence, performance submissions, and industry platforms. It lists what matters most to regulators: corporate announcements, governance, compliance, financial and non-financial performance, and financial inclusion. The frequency is continuous or need-based. The bank responds with transparent disclosures, robust compliance, responsible lending, NPA management, digitization, and third-party assured ESG disclosures. Shared value creation emphasizes compliance culture, ethical conduct, transparent governance, independent board committees, and regulatory adherence.

nodes.title: Employees
nodes.summary: The text explains why employees matter for organizational success and how the Bank supports them through a culture of values, inclusive policies, and practices. It lists communication channels (webcasts, newsletters, surveys, emails, management visits, Amber AI chatbot, town halls, training, appraisals, intranet, wellness programs, employee groups) with continuous/periodic frequency. It covers employee priorities—career growth, learning, health, inclusion, flexible work, leadership exposure, recognition, compensation—and the Bank’s responses: mobility program, learning resources, wellbeing ecosystem, feedback mechanisms, DEI promotion, AI tools, rewards, and leadership development. It concludes with Axis Bank’s commitment to over 1.04 lakh employees and key KPIs: 58.6 average L&D hours, 27.7% diversity, engagement scores, GIGA program, and 5,700+ internal mobility beneficiaries.

nodes.title: Industry & Peers
nodes.summary: This text outlines the Bank's engagement with industry peers and associations, emphasizing their impact and the Bank's connection methods. It details communication with trade associations, participation in IBA and multilateral platforms, and corporate seminars, with continuous or need-based frequency. Key priorities for stakeholders include policy advocacy, knowledge sharing, and collaboration. The Bank responds through formal representation on platforms like WEF, IBA, CII, BCCI, FICCI, and NASSCOM, engaging in thought leadership and advocacy on ESG, CSR, DE&I, and climate action. It highlights shared value creation in fiscal 2025, where leadership shaped ESG and climate agendas via national committees, demonstrating commitment to policy advocacy and thought leadership nationally and internationally. A reference to page 196 is provided for more details.

nodes.title: Communities & NGOs
nodes.summary: The text covers two stakeholder groups: Communities & NGOs and Rating Agencies. For Communities & NGOs, it explains their importance, connection methods (CSR programs, feedback, conferences, capacity building), frequency, key concerns (financial inclusion, education, environment, healthcare, etc.), responses (thematic CSR areas), and shared value creation with KPIs like ~10 lakh CSR participants across 32 states/UTs. For Rating Agencies, it details their influence on financial health and capital access, connection methods (meetings, emails, submissions), frequency, key concerns (financial profitability, ESG performance), responses (transparent reporting, improved profitability and ESG disclosures), and shared value creation, including strong credit/ESG ratings, reduced cost of capital, a $500M IFC blue finance loan, improved CAR and GNPA, and alignment with IR/BRSR frameworks.

nodes.title: Rating Agencies
nodes.summary: The text covers how credit and ESG rating agencies affect Axis Bank's financial health, capital access, interest rates, and cost of capital. It details engagement methods (one-on-one/group meetings, email correspondence, performance submissions) and frequency (periodic/need-based). It lists key concerns (financial parameters, profitability, ESG performance/reporting) and responses (transparent reporting, improved profitability/operations, better ESG disclosures/scores). It highlights shared value creation: strong ratings led to reduced cost of capital, better debt pricing, and green finance access, including a $500 million IFC loan for blue finance and green projects. It notes improved CAR by 44 bps and GNPA by 15 bps year-over-year, and alignment with <IR>/BRSR frameworks, reflecting resilient risk profile, governance, and long-term value creation.

nodes.title: Value Chain Partners
nodes.summary: The text outlines why value chain partners matter to a bank, how the bank connects with them through meetings, surveys, discussions, audits, and contracts, and the frequency of these interactions. It details partner priorities such as timely payouts, fair terms, ESG consciousness, ethical relations, and knowledge exchange, and the bank's responses including timely payments, equitable agreements, a Vendor Code of Conduct, trustworthy partnerships, and ESG focus. It also covers shared value creation via inclusive engagement, 97% local sourcing, ethical practices, awareness programs, and periodic assessments for compliance and improvement, under a materiality assessment section.

nodes.title: Identifying and prioritising key issues
nodes.summary: Axis Bank proactively identifies and manages Impacts, Risks, and Opportunities (IROs) for long-term sustainability and value creation. In fiscal 2025, it adopted a Double Materiality approach, following a 2022 stakeholder engagement and materiality assessment, identifying 15 IROs through internal assessment, sector research, peer review, benchmarking, and secondary sources. The assessment considers how Bank operations affect environment and people (impact materiality) and how IROs affect long-term value, financial performance, and resilience (financial materiality), including actual and potential, positive and negative, societal and environmental footprints across short, medium, and long term. The methodology aligns with CSRD, ESRS, BRSR, and <IR> frameworks. Continuous stakeholder engagement is emphasized, acknowledging diverse perspectives. The materiality matrix prioritizes matters such as regulatory compliance, risk management, fraud and money laundering prevention, privacy and data security, corporate governance, return on equity, customer experience, innovation, sustainable finance, employee engagement, climate change impact, financial inclusion, community engagement, policy advocacy, and diversity, equity, and inclusion.

nodes.title: Risk Management
nodes.summary:
Risk Management
What it Means
Robust risk management enhances the Bank’s resilience and drives sustainable growth. In today’s dynamic financial landscape, proactively managing both traditional financial and emerging ESG–related risks is key to navigating complexities and seizing opportunities.
Interlinkage with Value Creation
Our risk management framework empowers us to identify and address changing risks proactively. Supported by an independent Risk function, the Board maintains keen oversight on every aspect of risk management, ensuring transparency, accountability, and resilience.
FISCAL 2025 PERFORMANCE
» In–house ESG Rating model to augment borrower-level credit appraisal developed
» Built stress testing and scenario analysis capabilities in line with regulatory guidance and expectations

nodes.title: Corporate Governance & Ethical Business Conduct
nodes.summary: The text covers corporate governance and ethical business conduct, emphasizing their role in long-term success and trust-building through high governance standards, accountable leadership, and embedded ethics. It discusses a comprehensive ESG strategy aligning with stakeholder priorities, addressing climate challenges, and ensuring board oversight for transparency, fairness, and sustainable value creation. It highlights interlinkage with value creation via rigorous risk management, internal controls, and a robust governance framework ensuring regulatory compliance. Fiscal 2025 performance metrics include zero conflict of interest incidents, 15% women board representation, 61.54% independent directors, the first Indian bank to form an ESG Committee, and a top-tier IiAS leadership rating. It also references capital linkage, stakeholders impacted, SDGs impacted (negative/potential, positive/actual), and a materiality assessment from the Integrated Annual Report 2024-25.

nodes.title: Regulatory Compliance
nodes.summary:
Regulatory Compliance
Interlinkage with Value Creation
What it Means
Adherence to the regulatory framework is not just a legal obligation but essential to long– term value creation. As a leading financial institution in India, we navigate a complex and evolving regulatory environment, where any non–compliance can lead to financial penalties, legal repercussions, and reputational damage.
Our culture of compliance helps us mitigate risks better and bolsters business resilience and stakeholder confidence. Our stakeholders, including customers, investors, regulators, and the community, rely on our commitment to regulatory compliance and ethical conduct to mitigate potential risks.
Capital Linkage
Stakeholders Impacted

nodes.title: Fraud & Money Laundering–Prevention, Detection & Mitigation
nodes.summary: The text covers fraud and money laundering prevention, detection, and mitigation, emphasizing its importance for the Bank and financial system integrity, especially with digital banking growth. It discusses interlinkage with value creation through strong policies, processes, and advanced technologies to prevent fraud and money laundering in digital and physical realms. It presents Fiscal 2025 performance metrics: 98.9% of eligible employees trained in AML and related laws, 343 vigilance cases processed, and 427 officials subject to disciplinary action. It also mentions capital linkage, stakeholders impacted, SDG impact (negative potential, positive actual), and the Bank's value creation.

nodes.title: Privacy and Data Security
nodes.summary:
Privacy and Data Security
What it Means
Data privacy and security are fundamental to maintaining customer trust in today’s digital world. As a customer–centric organisation, we recognise that safeguarding personal data is critical to our reputation and business continuity. Data breaches can have severe consequences, making it essential to constantly strengthen our IT security measures to mitigate cyber threats and protect customer information.
Interlinkage with Value Creation
The Bank prioritises data security, investing in robust capabilities and adhering to stringent cyber security policies aligned with industry best practices and regulations. Our Information System Security Committee ensures regular assessment and validation of controls against cyber threats, aligning with ISO 27001 and PCI DSS standards.
FISCAL 2025 PERFORMANCE
» Best–in Class Cyber Security Score amongst peers from Pioneer cyber security rating agency
» Zero instances involving loss/ breach of customer data
SDG Impacted
Capital Linkage
Stakeholders Impacted

nodes.title: Return on Equity and Return to Shareholders
nodes.summary: The text covers Return on Equity (RoE) and Return to Shareholders as key financial performance indicators linked to sustainability and ESG integration for risk mitigation and long-term value creation. It details interlinkage with value creation through shareholder engagement and capital access. Fiscal 2025 performance metrics include consolidated RoE of 16.89%, consolidated RoA of 1.77%, net NPA of 0.33%, and operating profit of ₹42,105 crores. It also mentions capital linkage, SDG impact, and stakeholder impact (negative potential, positive actual), and references the Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 materiality assessment.

nodes.title: Customer Experience & Satisfaction
nodes.summary:
Customer Experience & Satisfaction
What it Means
An exceptional customer experience and satisfaction are fundamental to our success. With millions of customers relying on us, we are committed to safeguarding their interests, ensuring fairness, transparency, and the protection of their savings and investments. Customer feedback and effective grievance redressal are vital to improve our offerings and service delivery continuously.
Interlinkage with Value Creation
Leveraging our digital outreach, we seek customer feedback through regular satisfaction surveys, which allows us to gather valuable inputs that guide us in continuously improving our products and services. We also adhere to the RBI’s Customer Rights, Grievances Redressal, and Compensation Policy, ensuring fair treatment for our customers.
FISCAL 2025 PERFORMANCE
» 59 million customers
» 159 Retail Net Promoter Score on indexed baseline of 100, since inception of baseline (Q1FY23)

nodes.title: Sustainable Finance & Responsible Banking
nodes.summary: The text covers Sustainable Finance & Responsible Banking, defining it as integrating ESG factors into lending and investment to direct capital to high-impact projects, reduce risks, and meet demand for responsible practices while aligning with missions, SDGs, and low-carbon transition. It details interlinkage with value creation through the Bank's Sustainable Financing Framework (first Indian bank with Second Party Opinion), ESG Working Group oversight, ESG Policy for Lending, and Board-level climate risk integration. Fiscal 2025 performance highlights include progress toward the 2030 goal of INR 60,000 crores incremental lending (INR 48,412 crores reached), INR 22,160 crores green lending portfolio, 447 proposals assessed, and a $500 million Green Loan from IFC with a blue component. It also mentions capital linkage, stakeholders impacted, SDGs impacted, and value creation by the bank.

nodes.title: Employee Engagement, Development & Wellbeing
nodes.summary: The text covers Employee Engagement, Development & Wellbeing, detailing its meaning (attracting, developing, retaining talent via learning, engagement, wellbeing, mental health, work-life balance, safety, and inclusive culture), capital linkage (HR policy with career experiences, flexible work, outcome-driven metrics), stakeholders impacted, and Fiscal 2025 performance metrics (6 million+ learning hours, profit per employee D0.25 crores, 27.7% workforce diversity, 5,700+ internal mobility movements, D280 crores+ wellbeing spend). It also covers Innovation and Digitalisation, including its meaning (digital transformation, emerging technologies, personalized secure interactions), interlinkage with value creation (best-in-class technology, digital innovation, advanced analytics), capital linkage, stakeholders impacted, and Fiscal 2025 performance (30 million registered mobile banking users, ~15 million+ active users, app ratings 4.7/4.8, first Indian bank ISO certified for AWS/Azure cloud security). Both sections list SDGs impacted and materiality assessment notes.

nodes.title: Financial Inclusion, Literacy & Access
nodes.summary:
Financial Inclusion, Literacy & Access
What it Means
Interlinkage with Value Creation
Financial inclusion offers a vital opportunity to expand our reach and empower communities, reflecting our purpose of ‘Banking that leads to a more inclusive and equitable economy’. By broadening access to financial services, we aim to serve underserved populations and encourage greater participation in the formal economy. Financial literacy is a key enabler, equipping individuals with the knowledge to use financial services effectively, thus promoting their wellbeing and economic resilience.
The Bank’s efforts to promote financial inclusion have empowered millions of individuals, especially women, bringing them into the formal financial system. The efforts have also expanded their access to key social security schemes. By promoting financial access and protection, the Bank is strengthening its reach in rural markets, which is contributing to sustainable business growth and improved customer trust.
Capital Linkage
Stakeholders Impacted

nodes.title: Impact of Climate Change
nodes.summary: The text covers climate change as a multifaceted risk to the Bank, including financial risks from emissions, physical and transition risks, and financed emissions. It details the Bank's commitment to mitigation and adaptation through climate risk assessments, integrating sustainability into operations and credit appraisal for low-carbon transition and financial stability. It lists stakeholders impacted (negative potential, positive actual) and Fiscal 2025 performance metrics: 2.8 million women in microfinance rural lending, 13.79 lakh PM Jan Dhan Yojna customers, 4.13 lakh under Suraksha Bima, 1.31 lakh under Jeevan Jyoti, 10.05 lakh under Atal Pension; energy intensity 7.90 GJ/FTE, 140,345 tCO2e Scope 1 & 2 emissions, ~72,474 GJ renewable energy, ~3.27 million trees planted. It notes SDGs impacted and value creation by the bank.

nodes.title: Policy Advocacy and Thought Leadership
nodes.summary: The text covers the Bank's policy advocacy and thought leadership, detailing its active role in shaping financial regulations through expert insights at forums like WEF, SEBI, CII, and FICCI, and advocating for innovation, inclusivity, and resilience. It links these efforts to value creation via partnerships and summits that promote sustainable transformation and industry practice shaping. Fiscal 2025 performance notes membership in industry associations (ASSOCHAM, FICCI, CII, BCCI, IBA) and confirms no political contributions or spending. It references further details on page 196, and indicates capital linkage, stakeholder impact, and SDG impact (negative potential, positive actual).

nodes.title: Community Engagement & Development
nodes.summary:
Community Engagement & Development
What it Means
Interlinkage with Value Creation
Engaging with communities in the vicinity of our operations allows us to understand their needs and challenges. This enables us to develop targeted initiatives that drive positive social impact in reflection of our purpose of ‘Banking that leads to a thriving community and a healthier planet’.
A strong institutional framework governs the Bank’s CSR programs, which are overseen by the CSR Committee of the Board and aligned to Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013. We also draw inspiration from the UN SDGs, ensuring our work contributes to broader global development objectives. In fiscal 2025, our initiatives spanned geographies and themes from border villages to urban slums, natural resource management to cancer care, and grassroots sports to academic research.
Capital Linkage
Stakeholders Impacted

nodes.title: Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion
nodes.summary: This text outlines the Bank's Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DE&I) commitment, defining DE&I as creating a workplace with diverse representation, valued employees, and equitable opportunities to strengthen the Bank, drive innovation, and create long-term value. It links DE&I to value creation through empathy, purposeful action, belonging, and external community engagement for societal change. It covers capital linkage, stakeholders impacted (negative/potential and positive/actual), and a materiality assessment. Fiscal 2025 performance includes social impact metrics: 387,467 households via Sustainable Livelihoods, 7.7 lakh+ students in CSR education, 1.25 lakh women in financial literacy, and 381 athletes supported. Workforce metrics include 27.7% women representation, 34% hiring diversity, and ~33,000 rural women impacted via Axis Women in Motion. SDGs impacted and page number 67 are noted.

nodes.title: M D & C E O ’ S S TAT E M E N T
nodes.summary: M D & C E O ’ S S TAT E M E N T

nodes.title: Building a customer obsessed, resilient institution
nodes.summary: Amitabh Chaudhry, MD & CEO, reviews fiscal 2025 as pivotal, highlighting Axis Bank's GPS strategy, customer-centricity, and resilience. He details growth in high-RAROC segments, record branch expansion, deposit franchise improvement, leadership in wealth management and payments, and digital platforms. Financial performance includes ROA 1.77%, ROE 16.89%, core operating profit growth, healthy NIMs, and strong liquidity. The letter covers three core execution areas: becoming a resilient franchise, creating multiplicative forces, and building for the future. It discusses balancing growth with cost prudence, premiumisation, wholesale banking scale, balance sheet strength, technology investments, digital innovations, the 'One Axis' strategy, subsidiary performance, and focus on digital banking, Bharat Banking, and customer obsession. It also covers employee initiatives, ESG commitments, community impact, and forward-looking optimism for fiscal 2026.

nodes.title: E X T E R N A L E N V I R O N M E N T
nodes.summary: E X T E R N A L E N V I R O N M E N T

nodes.title: Navigating a shifting world order
nodes.summary: The text outlines the company's agile response to global risks while leveraging India's resilient economy, raising compliance thresholds for stakeholder benefit. It analyzes the economic slowdown in fiscal 2025 due to fiscal and monetary tightening: fiscal deficit reduction and election-related spending lull, and a decline in non-food credit growth driven by supply factors and regulatory concerns over loan-to-deposit ratios. It notes liquidity stress from RBI's forex interventions and credit slowdown, but highlights RBI's corrective actions—CRR cuts, liquidity injections, repo rate reductions, risk weight rollbacks, and looser LCR regulations—that have improved growth prospects. With inflation below 4%, policy focuses on stimulating growth, and the banking system remains well-capitalized with early signs of private investment rebound and controlled credit risks.

nodes.title: Global Economic Outlook
nodes.summary: The text outlines the global economic reset driven by the Trump administration's response to inequality, manufacturing decline, and multilateral institution misuse, leading to structural changes in trade, taxes, regulations, immigration, currency, and energy. This creates uncertainty and policy vacuums, with market volatility as the only limit. Uncertainty hinders global growth through deferred investment, fiscal tightening, and tighter financial conditions, posing credit, liquidity, market, and business risks. Opportunities for India include strong growth, minimal direct tariff impact, 'China+1' gains, infrastructure and electronics enhancements, robust service exports, and domestic real estate recovery boosting credit demand. The Bank's strategy balances prudence and opportunity, strengthening risk management while supporting 'China+1' sectors, global capability centres, SMEs, and real estate, with diversified portfolios and dynamic liquidity management.

nodes.title: Technology Evolution and Artificial Intelligence
nodes.summary: The text covers technology evolution driven by AI, machine learning, cloud computing, and blockchain reshaping finance. It highlights generative AI's role in productivity, decision-making, personalization, and innovation. Financial institutions integrate AI for credit assessment, fraud detection, and customer engagement, with digital adoption accelerated by mobile banking, UPI, and digital ecosystems. It discusses AI-first app experiences using real-time data and predictive intelligence for hyper-personalized services. India's digital transformation is detailed through JAM trinity, DigiLocker, UPI (150 billion transactions in FY2025), and SCBs leveraging AI, predictive analytics, automation, and cloud-native architectures. Milestones include CBDC pilot scaling and 24/7 payments. Risks listed are information/cyber security, technology, regulatory/compliance, and operational. Opportunities include scaling digital lending, collections, customer service via next-gen platforms, AI-led IT operations, marketing automation, conversational interfaces, and future-ready payments (UPI 2.0, CBDC). Strategic response includes SARAL for collections, Axis Digital Loans, 'open' platform, Adi GenAI chatbot, Kaleidoscope CXM, UPI 2.0 leadership, Gold on UPI, and CBDC pilots.

nodes.title: Climate Resilience and ESG Integration
nodes.summary: The text covers climate resilience and ESG integration in fiscal 2025, noting global regulatory focus on climate-related financial risks, including BCBS efforts to integrate climate risks into prudential standards. In India, the 'Amrit Kaal' vision drives investments in renewable energy, digital innovation, and sustainable infrastructure. SEBI mandates reasonable assurance on BRSR Core KPIs, and RBI introduces a climate-related financial disclosure framework. The strategic response includes climate risk stress testing, ESG disclosures, and scaling financing for positive outcomes. Risks include credit and operational risks. Opportunities include green bonds, transition finance, renewable energy lending, sustainability-linked loans, ESG-focused investor pools, and differentiated customer solutions. The bank is expanding ESG-aligned portfolios, raising green capital, engaging ESG investors, and offering tailored solutions. ESG governance is strengthened through board oversight, climate risk integration, sectoral exposure assessments, environmental risk screens, and client partnerships for transition finance.

nodes.title: Cyber Security and Data Privacy
nodes.summary: The text describes the fiscal 2025 cyber security and data privacy landscape, highlighting increasing complexity from digital adoption, sophisticated threats, and tighter regulations like DPDPA, SEBI's CSCRF, and enhanced incident reporting. It lists relevant risks (information/cyber, technology, regulatory, operational) and opportunities (enhancing digital trust and resilience via centralized threat intelligence like SSOC). It then outlines the strategic response: significant investment in multi-layered AI-driven security, real-time monitoring, cloud security certifications (ISO for AWS/Azure), BitSight ratings, and leveraging SSOC for threat intelligence sharing.

nodes.title: Talent and the Future of Work
nodes.summary: The text outlines talent cultivation, inclusion, and future-ready career paths as key to sustainable value, highlighting India's fiscal 2025 labor trends: digital fluency, AI readiness, hybrid work, and wellbeing. It details BFSI talent competition in technology, risk, ESG, cybersecurity, and analytics, with responses like digital learning, AI integration, internal mobility, and leadership development, plus prioritization of mental health and DE&I. It lists risks (operational, human capital, conduct) and opportunities (AI-assisted roles, engagement via mobility, and attracting future-ready talent). Axis Bank's initiatives are described: AI tools across the employee lifecycle, internal mobility platforms like Catalyst under Thrive, leadership programs, flexible work models (GIG-A, hybrid), and role-based digital learning, aiming for a resilient, future-ready workforce.

nodes.title: Regulatory and Policy Landscape
nodes.summary: The text outlines fiscal 2025 regulatory and policy changes in banking, highlighting RBI measures on cyber security, IT governance, climate disclosures, unsecured lending, and liquidity. It notes MeitY's Draft DPDP Rules 2025 for data protection and SEBI's BRSR Core assurance requirements for top listed entities. International momentum on AI governance, sustainable finance, and digital assets influenced India's policy. It identifies regulatory and compliance risk and opportunities in responsible digital innovation and ESG/cyber disclosure trust. The Bank's strategic response uses compliance-by-design across digital banking, AI, payments, and open banking, and enhances ESG and cyber security disclosures aligned with SEBI, RBI, and global best practices.

nodes.title: Making a Positive Change in Society
nodes.summary: The text outlines India’s fiscal 2025 social landscape, driven by digital adoption, rising aspirations, and focus on financial inclusion, education, healthcare, and sustainability. It notes intensified societal expectations for corporate responsibility, community engagement, and DE&I. The financial services sector fosters inclusive growth by expanding into Bharat markets, supporting small businesses and rural entrepreneurs, promoting digital financial literacy, and designing tailored products. Industry initiatives target livelihood generation, women’s empowerment, education, healthcare, and sustainable development. Relevant risks include business, operational, and reputation risks. Opportunities identified are expanding financial access, promoting inclusive growth for women and small businesses, and strengthening brand trust through sustainability and DE&I alignment. The Bank’s strategic response includes a Bharat Banking franchise, empowering women and MSMEs via credit, skills, and literacy, CSR programs in livelihood, education, and healthcare, and integrating sustainability and DE&I into corporate ethos to build stakeholder trust.

nodes.title: S T R AT E G Y I N A C T I O N
nodes.summary: S T R AT E G Y I N A C T I O N

nodes.title: Strengthening our House of GPS
nodes.summary: The text describes the evolution of the 'House of GPS' strategy, rooted in Growth, Profitability, and Sustainability. Launched in 2019, it unifies the Bank's team and aligns overall and business strategies. In 2021, two distinctiveness elements were added: 'Sparsh' (world-class customer experience) and 'Bharat' (profitable Bharat banking franchise), with a digital focus. In 2023, the Sustainability pillar was bolstered with four themes: Deposit Mobilisation, People Proposition, Operational Risk & Compliance Culture, and Execution Excellence. In 2024, 'Leveraging Emerging Technologies' (Generative AI and Intelligent Automation) was added as a key enabler. To support Execution Excellence, a dedicated project management team was established to deploy frameworks for improved project pace and efficiency. The House of GPS remains relevant, reflecting aspirations and prioritizing GPS strategy, key themes, and values.

nodes.title: GPS strategy
nodes.summary: The GPS strategy section outlines a plan for sustained financial outperformance through customer experience (Project 'Sparsh'), Bharat Banking profitability, and digital leadership. It details growth via deposit mobilization, high RAROC segments, and multiplicative forces; profitability with structural earnings improvement; and sustainability through governance, asset quality, and data analytics. Core values are listed. Business performance review shows 10% deposit growth, 14% term deposit growth, LCR of 119%, NII growth of 9%, operating profit growth of 13%, cost-to-assets ratio of 2.46%, focus segments CAGR of 26% and contribution rise to 22.7%, credit card issuance of 3.47 million with 13.7% market share, granular fee income at 89%, subsidiary PAT growth of 11%, wealth management AUM of ₹5.92 trillion, high app ratings, and 'One Axis' unification. Sustainability efforts cover risk management, technology, banking strategy, and ESG, including strengthened risk frameworks, GenAI adoption, Bharat Banking strengths, tools Sparsh and Siddhi, 'Thrive' people proposition, and ESG progress in governance, social, green operations, and sustainable financing.

nodes.title: Growth
nodes.summary: The text outlines a GPS strategy focused on sustained financial outperformance through customer experience (Project 'Sparsh'), Bharat Banking profitability, and digital leadership. It details growth via deposit mobilization, high RAROC segments, and multiplicative forces; profitability with structural earnings improvement; and sustainability through governance, asset quality, and data analytics. Core values are listed. Business performance review shows 10% deposit growth, 14% term deposit growth, LCR of 119%, NII growth of 9%, operating profit growth of 13%, cost-to-assets ratio of 2.46%, focus segments (SBB+SME+MC) CAGR of 26% and contribution rise to 22.7%, credit card issuance of 3.47 million with 13.7% market share, granular fee income at 89%, subsidiary PAT growth of 11%, wealth management AUM of ₹5.92 trillion, high app ratings, and 'One Axis' unification.

nodes.title: Growth
nodes.summary: The business performance review highlights strong growth with a 10% y-o-y increase in overall deposits and 14% y-o-y increase in term deposits, an average LCR of 119%, and significant scaling of focus segments (SBB, SME, MC) with a CAGR of 26% from FY2021 to FY2025, improving their contribution mix from 15.3% to 22.7%. Profitability showed 9% y-o-y growth in net interest income and 13% y-o-y growth in operating profit, with a stable cost-to-assets ratio of 2.46% in FY2025. The bank became the 4th largest credit card player, issuing 3.47 million cards and achieving a 13.7% CIF market share. Granular fees constituted 89% of overall fees, which grew 11% y-o-y. Operating subsidiaries' PAT grew 11% y-o-y with a 46% return on domestic investments. Wealth management AUM reached ₹5.92 trillion, growing 10% y-o-y. The 'open' app is highly rated (4.7 on Google Play, 4.8 on iOS). 'One Axis' unification and partnerships drove multiplicative forces. It became the first Indian bank ISO certified for AWS and Azure Cloud security and rolled out MS GenAI Co-pilot.

nodes.title: Sustainability
nodes.summary: The text outlines sustainability efforts across risk management, technology, banking strategy, and ESG. key_items: Real–Time Insights, Meaningful Interactions; Personalised Nudges for Deeper Conversations; 360–Degree Customer View; Enhanced Productivity and Delightful Service
nodes.summary: The text introduces 'Siddhi,' a mobile-first platform used by over 90,000 bank employees for real-time insights and personalized recommendations. It offers 30+ cross-sell journeys and 25+ service features, enabling on-the-go services like instant statements and real-time transactions. Advanced analytics deliver personalized nudges, boosting key metrics by ~30% and NPS by ~10 points. A 360-degree customer view helps bankers anticipate needs and identify cross-sell opportunities. Productivity tools include a daily calendar for prioritizing interactions. The platform blends technology with a human touch to enhance customer relationships and transform everyday banking.

nodes.title: SPARSH 2.0 Stories
nodes.summary: The text recounts a SPARSH 2.0 story where Branch Banking Manager Sivaprakash prevented a senior citizen from prematurely closing a ₹30 lakh FD after noticing signs of fraud. The customer was being instructed via WhatsApp by a fraudster. Sivaprakash alerted Operations Head Sasikala and Branch Head Kavitha Venkatesan. Despite initial resistance, the team explained similar scams, and when the fraudster called again, Kavitha insisted on a video call, causing the fraudster to hang up and erase chat history. The team's quick action saved the customer's life savings. The story concludes with praise from Senior Vice President P. Devarajan for Sivaprakash's presence of mind and the branch leadership's teamwork.

nodes.title: Remembering Sonam Chahal and her Legacy of Excellence
nodes.summary: The text memorializes Late Mrs. Sonam Chahal, a Deputy Manager at a bank's Gurugram branch, highlighting her exceptional service and role as a brand ambassador. It includes a colleague's recollection of her as special, a retired Air Chief Marshal's appreciation letter shared with her family, and a visit to her home to convey condolences and share memories of her compassion. The text emphasizes her kindness, work ethic, and joyful spirit as embodying cherished values, and concludes by celebrating her lasting inspiration to be better, kinder, and more dedicated.

nodes.title: ‘open’ by Axis Bank: Banking Transformed
nodes.summary: ‘open’ by Axis Bank is an autonomous digital banking entity contributing ~6% to overall business, focused on customer acquisition, expansion, and profitability. It offers end-to-end digital journeys across 30+ products including savings, investments, payments, and secured/unsecured lending, with intuitive, efficient, and secure onboarding and servicing. It achieved 15% asset growth and 47% liability growth in fiscal 2025, aims to lead in consumer lending, leverages Account Aggregator leadership for underwriting new-to-bank customers, and uses partnerships for digital loan origination. Customer experience features personalized nudges, ‘One View’ multi-bank/demat aggregation, and a transparent Benefits dashboard. Metrics: ~3 crore mobile banking registered customers, 47% credit cards issued digitally end-to-end, 15 million+ monthly active mobile banking users, app ratings 4.8 (Apple) and 4.7 (Google Play), tagline “Har raah dil se open.”

nodes.title: Capital Allocation & Risk–adjusted Returns
nodes.summary:
Capital Allocation & Risk–adjusted Returns
Our portfolio strategy is grounded in a disciplined focus on Risk–Adjusted Return on Capital (RAROC), ensuring capital efficiency and sustainable growth. This approach enables us to make informed decisions on capital and liquidity deployment, guided by three key pillars: Optimal yield placement, Return potential, and Predictive loss management.
We remain careful and selective in the retail unsecured segment, particularly personal loans and credit cards. Growth in this segment is driven by a balanced RAROC– led approach underpinned by advanced digital and data analytics capabilities. Simultaneously, we continue to strengthen our collections infrastructure with front–end tech enablement to enhance efficiency and outcomes.

nodes.summary: The text outlines the bank's community-centric initiatives under four focus areas: environmental sustainability, humanitarian relief, healthcare and nutrition, and sports. Environmental efforts include tree planting targets (3.27 million achieved, 8 million by 2030), mangrove restoration, agroforestry, human-wildlife conflict mitigation, and urban forests. Humanitarian relief covers flood and conflict response in Assam, Manipur, and Karnataka, impacting 7,278 households. Healthcare includes a ₹100 crore cancer care partnership with NCG, preventive screening by Indian Cancer Society, and a paediatric specialty centre at IISc. Sports initiatives support 224 athletes via Olympic Gold Quest and a judo development program for 157 athletes, including 53 female judokas.

nodes.title: Corporate Citizenship Initiatives
nodes.summary: The text covers Abhisaran 2025, a two-day multi-stakeholder forum celebrating the 'One Axis' CSR approach, bringing together bank officials, trustees, subsidiary board members, and over 70 NGO partners. It marked the completion of Mission2Million and launch of Mission4Million under the Sustainable Livelihood Program, expanding reach to 2 million more rural households. Day two featured sessions on navigating transition, Theory of Change, effective communication, systems thinking, value chains, health and nutrition, rural entrepreneurship, water governance, and youth employability. It also describes Axis Cares, an employee engagement platform for volunteering and financial contributions to various causes. Finally, it details Axis Bank's partnership with the government, including accreditations, tax collection, pension management, and PFMS and GeM contributions.

nodes.title: Partnering with the Government
nodes.summary: The Bank is a trusted partner for India's government sector, enhancing public finance, transparency, and citizen services. Accredited by key ministries and institutions, including a recent fourth accreditation from the Ministry of External Affairs for the Passport Seva Program, it supports collection for central taxes (CBDT, GST), employee welfare contributions (EPFO, ESIC), and state taxes in 15 states/UTs. It is the sole trustee bank for NPS under PFRDA, ranks among top PFMS performers, contributes to GeM, and delivers robust, secure, citizen-centric digital solutions.

nodes.title: Enabling Smart Governance and Urban Transformation
nodes.summary: This text outlines the Bank's role as a strategic partner to India's Smart City Mission, collaborating with municipal bodies, city administrations, and state governments to deliver tailored banking solutions. It highlights relationships with over half of India's Urban Local Bodies to strengthen urban governance. The Bank digitizes municipal operations for seamless payments, transparency, and civic engagement, embedding digital technology for responsive, sustainable, and inclusive cities. It has partnered with 27 Smart Cities for customized digital governance solutions, citing examples like Punjab m-SEWA (148 ULBs), Varanasi Nagar Nigam's QR-code property tax (3 lakh homes), and Rewa Municipal Corporation's app for certifications, grievances, revenue, and social security. It also mentions government partners: Varanasi Disaster Management's drone-based solutions and Jharkhand Jal Chajan Yojana's digital door-numbering. The text concludes with a count of 27 Smart Cities served and the tagline 'Har raah dil se open'.

nodes.title: Transforming Agriculture through Digi–culture
nodes.summary: The text discusses 'Digi-culture' transforming agriculture through trusted, transparent, tech-driven solutions. It highlights a flagship e-procurement platform for secure, timely farmer payments in government purchases, featuring real-time reconciliation, bulk transfers, and automation to reduce delays and fraud. It also covers Direct Benefit Transfers ensuring funds reach the right recipients on time. The text notes agricultural engagement across key states via partnerships with procurement agencies and cooperative bodies. It lists key fiscal 2025 engagements with organizations in Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, and Himachal Pradesh.

nodes.title: Health & Education
nodes.summary:
Health & Education
We support government institutions with banking solutions and intelligent, tech–enabled platforms that improve operational efficiency and citizen access.
In the healthcare ecosystem, we have introduced AI–based face recognition and integrated HRMS software for the Health Department of Bihar, addressing chronic challenges like medical personnel absenteeism. This smart solution has been replicated in Puducherry and Dadra & Nagar Haveli under the National Health Mission. We are also proud to be associated with transformative health initiatives,
including the Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission in Gujarat, which helps build future–ready and inclusive health systems.
Our support to the education sector includes digitised fee collection platforms for state education boards and institutions, making transactions secure, seamless, and accessible. Whether it is fee automation, reporting dashboards, or customised banking products, we serve as a reliable digital partner to schools, colleges, and universities such as the Directorate of Education, Goa.

nodes.title: Driving Digital Mobility Infrastructure
nodes.summary:
Driving Digital Mobility Infrastructure
We partner with urban authorities to make vehicular movement frictionless, efficient, and future–ready. We pioneered India’s first AI+FASTag–enabled smart parking system in collaboration with the Guwahati Metropolitan Development Authority. This fully automated solution eliminates manual ticketing, introduces contactless entry and exit, and enhances overall user convenience, setting a new benchmark for urban mobility.
In Delhi, we were selected as the sole acquiring bank for Digital Stand Fee Collection at Inter–State Bus Terminals (ISBTs), using RFID–based FASTag technology. This initiative streamlines the collection of parking and entry fees, reduces congestion, enhances transparency, and promotes cashless transit ecosystems.

nodes.title: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) Initiatives
nodes.summary: The Bank strengthens India's DBT ecosystem by ensuring transparent, prompt fund delivery to beneficiaries. Its platforms support various state and centrally sponsored schemes covering women and child development, tribal welfare, and urban transformation, with real-time validations and direct account credit to eliminate leakages. Fiscal 2025 DBT services include Maharashtra's Krantijyoti Savitribai Phule Bal-Sangopan Yojana, Assam's Chief Minister's Atmanirbhar Asom Abhijan, Tamil Nadu's Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department, AMRUT, and Swachh Bharat Mission. The text also highlights India's first AI+FASTag smart parking system launched in Guwahati, and RFID-FASTag-enabled stand fee and parking collection at Delhi ISBTs.

nodes.title: Driving environmental impact through action and accountability
nodes.summary: Axis Bank outlines its environmental stewardship approach, integrating responsibility into operations, growth, and value creation through carbon footprint reduction, resource conservation, and sustainable finance. It links material issues (M8, M12), capital, and SDGs, and notes its environmental footprint from branch energy, diesel generators, and paper use. Fiscal 2025 highlights include a ₹22,160 crore green lending portfolio, 447 ESG-assessed proposals via ESDD, four large offices fully powered by renewable energy, ~8.78% renewable energy use, and ~3.27 million saplings planted under CSR initiatives such as Miyawaki and other tree plantation programs. The bank leverages digital transformation, best practices, and green technology investments to reduce its footprint.

nodes.title: Energy & Emissions
key_items: Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency Initiatives
Operational Energy Efficiency; Green Data Centres (Bengaluru)
nodes.summary: The text outlines a company's decarbonisation strategy aligned with SBTi, targeting a 3.5% reduction in emission intensity per FTE by fiscal 2027 from a fiscal 2023 baseline. It details monitoring of Scope 1 (diesel, refrigerant leaks), Scope 2 (electricity), and Scope 3 (air travel, local transport, paper, employee commute) emissions. Renewable energy initiatives include a 2 MW solar plant in Solapur, ~1 MW solar PPA for Bengaluru Data Centre, and 100% renewable energy at top three offices. A Centralised Energy Management System (CEMS) enables remote monitoring. Operational efficiency measures cover APFC panels, LED systems, EV charging, star-rated ACs, motion sensors, advanced cooling, BMS-integrated sensors, modular UPS, and green building certification. Fiscal 2025 impact: 2,222 tCO2e avoided from Solapur solar and 7,321 tCO2e from Bengaluru Data Centre renewables.

nodes.title: Water Conservation
nodes.summary: The text covers water conservation efforts including efficient management, recycling, and responsible usage, with actions like rainwater harvesting and innovative recycling to reduce water footprint. It lists specific measures: closed-loop water system at Bengaluru Data Centre, rainwater harvesting at Axis House Mumbai, and sensor-based washbasins, aerators, and bio-blocks at select offices. It also reports key achievements for fiscal 2025: annual energy savings of 3.87 million kWh from CEMS and efficiency interventions, emissions avoided of ~1,277 tCO2e from digital banking, Scope 1 emissions of 11,347.37 tCO2e, Scope 2 emissions of 140,344.99 tCO2e, Scope 3 emissions of 41,566.90 tCO2e, and rainwater harvested annually of ~5.5 KL at Axis House Mumbai and ~275 KL at Bengaluru Data Centre.

nodes.title: Responsible Waste Management
nodes.summary: The text outlines responsible waste management practices focused on segregation, recycling, and digital solutions to reduce environmental impact and divert waste from landfills. Key fiscal 2025 achievements include recycling about 220.60 metric tons of dry waste, 396.89 metric tons of e-waste PAN-India, and 34.48 metric tons of battery waste through authorized vendors. Measures feature centralized systems at Axis House, Mumbai and major offices to recycle dry waste into usable stationery, collaborations with certified vendors for safe e-waste disposal nationwide, and digital banking initiatives (digital account opening, e-statements, e-welcome kits) that save approximately 15 million sheets of paper annually.

nodes.title: Habitat Restoration Activities
nodes.summary: The Bank's habitat restoration and tree planting initiatives under ESG and CSR commitments, including achieving ~2.02 million trees by March 2025 (target 2 million by fiscal 2026), augmenting to ~3.27 million trees, and a new target of ~8 million trees by 2030. It also includes footnotes on emission calculation boundaries (India operations only, excluding subsidiaries), waste management reporting scope across specific office counts by waste type, and estimation bases for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions.

nodes.title: Impetus to Retail EV Financing
nodes.summary: The Bank set a FY2021 target of 5% EV share in retail two-wheeler loans by March 2024, reaching 3.62% cumulatively since October 2021, with EV sales penetration above 5% in 9 of 12 months in FY2024 and 5.53% for the year. It revised targets to 6% EV revenue share in two-wheeler and 4% in four-wheeler passenger loan portfolios by 2027, achieving 7.14% and 2.92% respectively in FY2024–25. The Bank offers up to 0.5% interest rate discounts, special OEM deals with higher payouts, and scaled partnerships with dealers and manufacturers. It provided 12,704 EV loans in FY2025 and communicated intent to set fresh EV targets to the ESG Committee.

key_items: Anti–corruption and Anti–bribery; Conflict of Interest Policy; Human Rights; Compliance; Subsidiary Governance
nodes.summary: This document outlines Axis Bank's policies and frameworks for responsible governance. It details the Code of Conduct and Ethics, corporate governance policies (POSH, Whistleblower, Conflict of Interest, Staff Accountability), Tax Policy, Whistleblower and Vigil Mechanism (with complaint statistics), Anti-corruption and Anti-bribery measures (vigilance function, cases processed, disciplinary actions), Conflict of Interest Policy, Human Rights Policy, Compliance framework, Subsidiary Governance (SGC, EGRMC, Board oversight), ESG Governance (ESG Committee, Steering Committee, DEI Council, meetings), and Fraud Risk Management (FCI unit, key initiatives, customer awareness, employee engagement, corporate client advisory, future-ready fraud defence).

nodes.title: Resilience through purposeful risk stewardship
nodes.summary: The text outlines a robust Risk Management Framework with independent oversight by the Board and Risk Management Committee (RMC), covering credit, liquidity, market, operational, compliance, and reputation risks. It details the risk governance structure, including the CRO, RMD, and various committees, emphasizing autonomy and accountability. It highlights proactive focus areas like credit-led retail growth, cyber security, technological resilience, sustainability, and managing subsidiary, operational, vendor, fraud, and digital risks. Key RMC achievements in Fiscal 2025 include enhanced stress testing, group risk oversight, cyber security, and model risk. Key focus areas for Fiscal 2026 include risk appetite governance, unsecured lending, cyber security, risk culture, and digital/technology risk.

nodes.title: Other Components of Risk Management
nodes.summary: The text covers three other components of risk management: Internal Audit, Business Continuity Plan, and Fraud Detection and Mitigation. Internal Audit independently evaluates controls, risk, and governance, reporting to the Board and following RBI RBIA standards, with technology-driven audits and skill-building. The Business Continuity Plan is overseen by the BCPMC, ensuring implementation, testing, and integration of insights for seamless contingency response. Fraud detection and mitigation involve a comprehensive policy, real-time transaction monitoring, AML software for alerts, and a dedicated system for card fraud prevention.

nodes.title: Risk Management Approach
nodes.summary: The text outlines a bank's risk management approach, emphasizing trust, transparency, and resilience. It details four foundational pillars: risk philosophy (shared responsibility, compliance, and reputation), risk identification and mitigation (vigilant monitoring, reporting via ICAAP and Risk Dashboards, collaboration with business units), risk appetite and policies (RMC-approved appetite, Board-approved policies, executive committees and RMD implementation), and risk culture (leadership by example, openness, accountability, compliance function). It then covers specific initiatives for key material risks: credit risk (asset quality, concentration risk, capital linkage, SDGs, mitigation via internal ratings for wholesale and scorecards for retail with independent validation) and market risk (interest rate, equity, forex; capital linkage, SDGs, mitigation via comprehensive framework, independent oversight, statistical measures like VaR, stress tests, back tests, scenario analysis, and non-statistical measures like position limits, MTM, stop-loss; VaR calculation details). Risk status is also mentioned.

nodes.title: Credit and Market Risk Management Initiatives
nodes.summary: The page covers specific risk management initiatives for credit and market risk. Credit risk is defined as potential loss from counterparty default, with management focused on asset quality and concentration risks at individual and portfolio levels, including internal ratings for wholesale banking and product-specific scorecards for retail banking with independent validation. Market risk arises from on- and off-balance sheet positions due to market price movements, including interest rate, equity price, and foreign exchange rates, with trading and investment activities as primary sources. Mitigation measures include a comprehensive framework, independent oversight by RMD, statistical tools like VaR, stress tests, back tests, and scenario analysis, plus non-statistical measures such as position limits, MTM evaluations, and stop-loss limits. VaR calculation uses historical simulation at 99% confidence over a one-day holding period based on a 250-day horizon, with continuous back and stress testing. Capital linkage, SDG impacts, and risk status are also noted.

nodes.title: Market Risk
nodes.summary: The text covers key material risks: credit risk (counterparty failure, asset quality, concentration management, with capital linkage and SDG impact) and market risk (losses from market price movements, including interest rate, equity, and foreign exchange, with capital linkage and SDG impact). It details mitigation measures for wholesale banking (internal ratings for risk acceptance, exposure limits, sanctioning, pricing, review) and retail banking (product-specific scorecards, independent validation of credit models). Market risk mitigation includes a comprehensive framework, independent oversight by RMD, statistical measures (VaR, stress tests, back tests, scenario analysis) and non-statistical measures (position limits, MTM, stop-loss). VaR calculation uses historical simulation at 99% confidence, one-day holding, 250-day horizon, with back and stress testing. Risk status is noted.

nodes.title: Liquidity Risk
nodes.summary: The text covers liquidity risk, defined as a bank's inability to meet cash and collateral obligations, with mitigation measures including an Asset Liability Management Policy, intraday liquidity, stress testing, contingency funding, and branch-level liquidity. Monitoring involves gap analyses, key ratios, stress tests, and oversight by ALCO and RMC, with regulatory adherence to RBI and Basel III (LCR, NSFR). It also addresses information and cyber security risks from unauthorized access, breaches, and malware, with mitigation through a comprehensive program governed by the Information System Security Committee, aligned with NIST, ISO 27001:2013, and PCI DSS. Proactive measures include security checks, vulnerability assessments, penetration tests, multi-layered defense, and 24x7 SOC monitoring. Capital linkage and SDG impacts are noted.

nodes.title: Information and Cyber Security Risks
nodes.summary: The text covers two key material risks: liquidity risk and information/cyber security risks. For each, it defines the risk, notes capital linkage and SDG impact, and lists mitigation measures. Liquidity risk mitigation includes an ALM policy framework, monitoring via gap analyses and stress tests, oversight by ALCO and RMC, and regulatory adherence to RBI and Basel III (LCR, NSFR). Cyber risk mitigation includes a governance framework aligned with NIST, ISO 27001, and PCI DSS, proactive security measures like vulnerability assessments and penetration tests, defence-in-depth with 24x7 SOC monitoring, and collaboration with regulators and industry. Risk status indicators are also mentioned.

nodes.title: Operational Risk
nodes.summary: The text covers operational risks from inadequate controls in internal processes, personnel, systems, and external events. It details climate risk categories: transition risks from policy, regulation, technology, and consumer preferences, and physical risks including chronic (temperature, precipitation, agriculture, sea levels) and acute (heat waves, floods, cyclones, wildfires) impacts. It outlines mitigation measures: a comprehensive ORM policy and governance framework, thorough evaluation with committee oversight, global framework alignment with TCFD-aligned disclosures per RBI guidelines, climate risk integration monitored by the ESG Committee, and development of climate scenario analysis and stress testing. Additional measures include robust governance and strategic oversight since 2021 for climate-related and ESG risks, a measurement system for continuous enhancement, climate risk dashboards, ESG e-modules and training, and collaboration with industry bodies and regulators. Risk status and capital linkage are also mentioned.

A defence-in-depth approach and 24x7 Security Operations Centre monitoring guard against unauthorized access, hacking, and data loss, aligned with industry best practices and regulatory guidelines to reinforce customer confidence across banking channels.

nodes.title: Measures for Proactive Detection of Cyber Threats

nodes.title: ANNUAL REPORT ON CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY ACTIVITIES
nodes.summary: This Annual CSR Report outlines the company's CSR policy, committee composition, and third-party impact assessments of five projects. Project 1 assessed a financial literacy program for 2,326 women, showing improved financial tracking and savings awareness but gaps in insurance subscription. Project 2 evaluated a mobile-van financial literacy program across 18 locations, finding high recall for basic banking topics but lower for digital topics, with positive post-training budgeting behavior. Project 3 assessed 300 congenital heart surgeries, reporting 100% surgical success, improved health and school resumption, and high family satisfaction. Project 4 evaluated a mid-day meal program for 1 lakh children, showing high satisfaction, improved concentration, attendance, and health. Project 5 assessed tuition, hostel, and infrastructure support at a Manipur school, noting reduced financial stress and improved attendance. The report also includes CSR financial disclosures and signatories.

nodes.title: Impact Assessment Project 1
nodes.summary: This Annual Report on CSR Activities outlines the company's CSR policy, emphasizing inclusive and sustainable development through livelihoods, education, financial inclusion, environmental sustainability, and humanitarian relief. It details the CSR Committee's composition and meeting attendance, provides website links for CSR policy and projects, and summarizes third-party impact assessments of five projects. The financial literacy program's assessment, based on surveys of 2,326 women and a control group, shows high recall, improved financial tracking, savings awareness, insurance understanding, and hygiene practices, though gaps in insurance subscription remain. Overall, the program successfully enhanced financial literacy and planning.

nodes.title: Impact Assessment Project 2
nodes.summary: The text describes an impact assessment of a Financial Literacy Program by CSC Academy and Axis Bank using 20 mobile vans operated by VLEs to educate rural India via video content. The fiscal 2023 assessment covered 18 locations, surveying 455 participants through interviews and feedback. Key findings include high recall for bank account opening (77%), budgeting (71%), and insurance schemes (69%); lower recall for digital topics like UPI registration (55%) and safe banking app use (62%); fraud awareness at 69%; strong understanding of account documents (80%) and savings accounts (76%); lower comprehension of loan usage (66%) and BHIM app (54%); life insurance awareness at 72% and government schemes at 71%. Post-training, 62% started budgeting and 64% discussed financial planning with families. The program positively impacted financial literacy, with recommendations to strengthen VLE training and responsiveness.

nodes.title: Impact Assessment Project 3
nodes.summary: This impact assessment evaluates Axis Bank's partnership with Sri Sathya Sai Health & Education Trust, which funded 300 congenital heart surgeries for children at Sri Sathya Sai Sanjeevani Hospital, Raipur, during fiscal 2023. Patients came from 15 Indian states, and the program provided holistic care including preoperative, surgical, and postoperative follow-up. Findings draw on quantitative data, a review of 60 patient records, interviews with 32 parents and children, and qualitative input from cardiologists, surgeons, caseworkers, chief medical officers, and FGDs with the hospital's Impact Assessment and Counselling Team. Key results include a 100% surgical success rate; 96.8% health improvement; 82.76% school resumption; 96.8% regular follow-up; 84.38% active physical participation; 93.76% family satisfaction; 81.26% emotional well-being improvement; and 90% of families earning under ₹20,000 monthly. Stakeholders noted reduced mortality and complications through best practices like intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography, with children returning to school and families experiencing renewed hope and reduced financial burden.

nodes.title: Impact Assessment Project 4
nodes.summary: This impact assessment evaluates Axis Bank and Akshaya Patra Foundation's Mid-Day Meal program, which provided meals to about 1 lakh children across Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Karnataka, and Odisha from December 2022 to March 2023. Using a retrospective post-then-pre mixed-methods design, it measured nutrition, participation, learning outcomes, and satisfaction. The survey covered 150 students from 15 schools in Odisha and Karnataka, with 60.6% females and 87.9% from BPL families. Key findings: 96% satisfied with meal quantity; 100% of teachers noted improved concentration; 87.5% said stopping MDM would hurt attendance; 85% of teachers found meals satisfactory; 62% of students rated taste very good (71% in Karnataka); and health improved with more energy, fewer sick days, and better attendance. Overall, stakeholders highlight significant positive impacts on nutrition, attendance, and academic performance.

nodes.title: Impact Assessment Project 5

It details a mixed-method evaluation with qualitative surveys and interviews, and key findings on reduced financial stress, improved attendance due to hostel facilities, and benefits of the science lab and digital classrooms. nodes.title: Retail Banking
nodes.summary: The text outlines the Bank's Retail Banking franchise as a key growth driver, built on customer-centricity, differentiated products, and a wide distribution network.
