(B) Investment Reserve Account; Closing Balance; V. Balance In Profit & Loss Account
V. Balance In Profit & Loss Account
nodes.summary: Schedule 2 details Reserves and Surplus with opening balances, additions, deductions, and closing balances for statutory reserve, capital reserve, share premium account, revenue and other reserves (including special reserve, investment reserve account, general reserve, foreign currency translation reserve, investment fluctuation reserve, available for sale reserve, and cash flow hedge reserve), and balance in profit & loss account, presented in thousands for the years ended 31-03-2025 and 31-03-2024, with cross-references to other schedules.

nodes.title: Schedule 3 - Deposits
nodes.summary: The text presents Schedules 3 to 7 from a financial document, detailing deposits, borrowings, other liabilities and provisions, cash and balances with RBI, and balances with banks and money at call and short notice. It includes breakdowns by category, such as demand, savings, and term deposits, domestic and overseas branches, and provides comparative figures as of March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024, in thousands of rupees, along with explanatory notes on secured borrowings, subordinated debt, additional tier I bonds, and deposits under lien.

nodes.title: Schedules 4-6: Borrowings, Other Liabilities, and Cash Balances
key_items: Schedule 6 - Cash and Balances with Reserve Bank of India
nodes.summary: The page presents three financial statement schedules with comparative figures as of 31-03-2025 and 31-03-2024 in thousands. Schedule 4 covers borrowings in India (from RBI, other banks, other institutions/agencies) and outside India, plus total and secured borrowings, with footnotes on subordinated debt and Additional Tier I Bonds. Schedule 5 lists other liabilities and provisions: bills payable, inter-office adjustments, interest accrued, general provision on standard assets, MTM loss on forex/derivative contracts, provision for tax, and others, with totals. Schedule 6 details cash and balances with RBI: cash in hand, current account balances, and other account balances (including reverse repo under LAF), with totals.

nodes.title: Schedule 7 - Balances with Banks and Money at Call and Short Notice
nodes.summary: Schedule 7 details balances with banks and money at call and short notice, split into India and outside India. For India: balances with banks in current and other deposit accounts, plus money at call and short notice with banks and other institutions, with totals for 2025 and 2024. For outside India: current accounts, other deposit accounts, and money at call and short notice, with totals for both years. It provides grand totals for both years, all in thousands of rupees, as part of standalone financial statements.

nodes.title: Schedule 8 - Investments
key_items: I. Investments in India in -; II. Investments outside India in -
nodes.summary: Schedule 8 - Investments lists investments in India (government securities, other approved securities, shares, debentures/bonds, subsidiaries/JVs/associates, and others including mutual funds, security receipts, AIFs, VCFs, REITs, InvITs, PTCs, and PE funds) and outside India (government securities including local authorities, subsidiaries/JVs abroad, and others including equity shares and bonds), with totals and grand total for March 31, 2025 and 2024 in thousands. It includes a note that government securities include pledged securities of face value ₹1,70,046.36 crores (previous year ₹1,52,280.19 crores) for fund transfer, clearing, repo, and margin requirements.

nodes.title: Schedule 9 - Advances
nodes.summary: Schedule 9 - Advances presents a detailed breakdown of advances in India and outside India as of March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024, in thousands. It categorizes domestic advances into bills purchased and discounted, cash credits/overdrafts/loans repayable on demand, and term loans, with totals. Further classification includes secured by tangible assets, covered by bank/government guarantees, and unsecured, with totals. Advances are also split by priority sector, public sector, banks, and others. Advances outside India cover due from banks and due from others, with subcategories like bills purchased and discounted, syndicated loans, and others. Footnotes clarify netting of borrowings under IBPC, inclusion of advances against book debts and L/Cs issued by other banks. Grand totals reconcile with the sum of domestic and foreign advances.

nodes.title: Schedule 10 - Fixed Assets
nodes.summary: Schedule 10 - Fixed Assets presents a tabular breakdown of fixed assets in thousands of rupees for the years ending 31-03-2025 and 31-03-2024. It covers three sections: I. Premises, detailing gross block (opening cost, additions, deductions, total), depreciation (opening, charge, deductions, depreciation to date), and net block; II. Other fixed assets (including furniture, fixtures, and intangibles), with gross block (opening, additions/deletions from Citibank India Consumer Business acquisition, additions, deductions, total), depreciation (opening, charge, deductions, depreciation to date), and net block; and III. Capital Work-In-Progress (including capital advances). A grand total (I+II+III) is provided. A footnote indicates that additions include exchange rate fluctuation movements.

nodes.title: Schedule 11 - Other Assets
nodes.summary: Schedule 11 details Other Assets as of 31-03-2025 and 31-03-2024, in thousands. Categories include inter-office adjustments (net), interest accrued, tax paid in advance/TDS (net of provisions), stationery and stamps, non-banking assets acquired in satisfaction of claims, MTM gain on forex and derivative contracts, and others. It provides monetary values for each category and totals: 669,529,740 as of 31-03-2025 and 604,740,043 as of 31-03-2024. Notes clarify that non-banking assets are net of provisions of ₹1,855.85 crores (both years) on land, others include deferred tax assets of ₹4,441.01 crores (previous year ₹5,312.30 crores) per Schedule 18 (2.8), and Priority Sector Shortfall Deposits of ₹14,450.47 crores (previous year ₹21,557.10 crores).

nodes.title: Schedule 12 - Contingent Liabilities
nodes.summary: Schedule 12 details the Bank's contingent liabilities, listing claims not acknowledged as debts, liabilities for partly paid investments, outstanding forward and derivative contracts (notional amounts), guarantees given on behalf of constituents in and outside India, acceptances, endorsements, other obligations, and other contingent liabilities. It provides comparative amounts in thousands as of March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024, with a grand total, and references Schedule 18 (2.14).

nodes.title: Schedules Forming Part of the Profit & Loss Account
nodes.summary: This section presents schedules forming part of the Profit & Loss Account for the year ended 31 March 2025, detailing Interest Earned, Other Income, Interest Expended, and Operating Expenses, along with comparative figures. It also includes significant accounting policies covering the bank's background, basis of preparation, and changes effective 1 April 2024. Key areas include investment classification (HTM, AFS, FVTPL) and valuation under RBI Investment Direction 2023, with transition adjustments; accounting for repos, advances (including NPA classification, provisioning, and restructuring), country risk, securitisation, loan transfers, PSLCs, and foreign currency translation. It further covers foreign exchange and derivative contracts, revenue recognition, fixed assets and depreciation, impairment, non-banking assets, lease transactions, employee benefits (short-term, defined benefit, defined contribution), reward points, taxation (current and deferred), share issue expenses, corporate social responsibility, earnings per share, employee stock options, provisions and contingencies, dividend accounting, cash equivalents, and segment reporting.

nodes.title: Schedules Forming Part of the Profit & Loss Account (intro)
nodes.summary: The text presents schedules from a Profit & Loss Account for the year ended 31 March 2025, including comparative figures for 2024. Schedule 13 details Interest Earned from advances, investments, RBI balances, and others. Schedule 14 covers Other Income sources like commissions, investment profits, asset sales, and dividends. Schedule 15 shows Interest Expended on deposits, RBI borrowings, and others. Schedule 16 lists Operating Expenses such as employee costs, rent, depreciation, and other expenditures. The document also includes significant accounting policies covering the bank's background, basis of preparation, use of estimates, and changes in accounting policies effective 1 April 2024.

nodes.title: 4.1 Classification and Valuation of Investments
nodes.summary: The text details the Bank's adoption of the RBI Investment Direction, 2023, effective 1 April 2024, including transition provisions: transfer of ₹242.29 crores from Investment Reserve Account to general reserve, and ₹1,217.86 crores (net of tax) to general reserve from reversal of depreciation provision and carrying value adjustments, increasing net worth. It also covers compliance with the direction: aggregation of valuation gains/losses for AFS investments with net appreciation of ₹110.39 crores (net of tax) recognized in AFS Reserve, and fair valuation of FVTPL securities with net gain of ₹700.51 crores recognized in Profit and Loss Account for the year ended 31 March 2025. Previous year figures are not comparable. The text appears in financial statements and precedes significant accounting policies.

nodes.title: 5.1 Investments
nodes.summary: This text outlines significant accounting policies for investments in FY25 under RBI Investment Direction, 2023. It covers classification at acquisition into Held to Maturity (HTM), Available for Sale (AFS), and Fair Value through Profit and Loss (FVTPL) with Held for Trading (HFT) as a subcategory. Balance sheet disclosure categories are specified: six for India (Government Securities, Other Approved Securities, Shares, Debentures and Bonds, Subsidiaries/Joint Ventures/Associates, Others) and three for outside India (Government Securities, Subsidiaries/Joint Ventures abroad, Others). Accounting is on settlement date except equity shares on trade date. Criteria for HTM (intention to hold to maturity and SPPI), AFS (collecting cash flows and selling, SPPI, irrevocable election for equity), and FVTPL (residual, with HFT for short-term resale, price movements, arbitrage, hedging; listed equities, repo-style transactions, market-making, fund investments in HFT; unlisted equities in Non-HFT) are detailed.

nodes.title: Classification
nodes.summary: The section outlines accounting policies under RBI Investment Direction, 2023, covering investment classification into HTM, AFS, and FVTPL (with HFT subcategory), balance sheet disclosure categories for India and outside India, and settlement versus trade date accounting. It details conditions for each category, including HTM at cost with amortization of premium/discount and capital reserve appropriation for gains; AFS fair valuation with gains/losses in AFS Reserve (CET 1 capital) and transfer rules on sale/maturity; and FVTPL fair valuation through profit and loss. It addresses investments in subsidiaries, associates, and joint ventures at acquisition cost, fair value hierarchy, valuation norms for various instruments, asset classification and provisioning for NPIs, reclassification, and short sales of government securities.

nodes.title: Classification (intro)
nodes.summary: The text outlines significant accounting policies for investments under RBI Investment Direction, 2023. It covers classification into HTM, AFS, and FVTPL (with HFT subcategory), balance sheet disclosure categories for India (six) and outside India (three), and settlement versus trade date accounting. It details conditions for HTM, AFS (including irrevocable equity election), and FVTPL (HFT and Non-HFT criteria). It addresses investments in subsidiaries, associates, and joint ventures as a separate category. Initial recognition at fair value, acquisition cost treatment (brokerage, broken period interest, weighted average cost), and Day 1 gain/loss rules (quoted, Level 3, debt, unquoted equity deferral/amortization) are explained, with a mention of subsequent measurement.

nodes.title: a. Investments classified under the HTM category
nodes.summary:
a. Investments classified under the HTM category
Investments held in HTM category are carried at cost and are not Mark-to-Market (MTM) after initial recognition. Any discount or premium on the investments under HTM category is amortised over the remaining life of the instrument. The amortised amount is reflected under item II ‘Income on Investments’ of Schedule 13: ‘Interest Earned’ with a contra in Schedule 8: ‘Investments’.
Realised gains on sale of investments in HTM category are recognised in the Profit and Loss Account and subsequently appropriated to the Capital Reserve Account (net of taxes and transfer to statutory reserves) in accordance with the RBI guidelines. Realised losses are recognised in the Profit and Loss Account.

nodes.title: b. Investments classified under AFS category
nodes.summary: The text covers the accounting treatment for investments under the Available for Sale (AFS) category, including fair valuation, amortization of discounts/premiums on debt securities, and reflection in financial statements (Schedule 13 and Schedule 8). It details aggregation of net valuation gains/losses, crediting/debiting to AFS Reserve without routing through Profit & Loss, and its classification as CET 1 capital with restrictions on dividend and coupon distribution. It explains transfer of accumulated gains/losses to Profit & Loss on sale or maturity of debt instruments, and for designated equity instruments, transfer of gains/losses to Capital Reserve per RBI Investment Direction, 2023.

nodes.title: c. Investments classified under FVTPL category
nodes.summary:
c. Investments classified under FVTPL category
Investments held under FVTPL category are fair valued and the net gain or loss arising on such valuation is directly credited or debited to the Profit and Loss Account. Any discount or premium on the debt securities under FVTPL category is amortised over the remaining life of the instrument. The amortised amount is reflected in the financial statements under item II ‘Income on Investments’ of Schedule 13: ‘Interest Earned’ with a contra in Schedule 8: ‘Investments’.

nodes.title: d. Investments in Subsidiaries, Associates and Joint Ventures
nodes.summary: The text details accounting policies for investments in subsidiaries, associates, and joint ventures, including measurement at acquisition cost and amortization of discounts/premiums. It outlines fair value hierarchy (Levels 1-3) and valuation norms per RBI guidelines for various instruments: quoted investments, discounted instruments, mutual funds, venture capital funds, AIFs, unquoted government securities, bonds, debentures, preference shares, PTCs, unquoted equity shares, private equity funds, REITs/INVITs, and security receipts. It also covers investment asset classification and provisioning for NPIs, reclassification between categories, and short sales of government securities.

nodes.title: Classification
nodes.summary: The text details investment classification under RBI guidelines: HFT, AFS, and HTM, including transfer rules. It covers balance sheet disclosure categories for India and abroad, accounting dates, transfer between categories, and acquisition cost treatment (brokerage, broken period interest, weighted average method). Valuation rules are provided for HTM (amortization, impairment), AFS/HFT (mark-to-market, depreciation recognition), and specific instruments like T-bills, mutual funds, unquoted securities, REITs/INVITs, VCFs/AIFs, and security receipts. Disposal treatment for HTM and AFS/HFT categories and short sale transactions are also described.

nodes.title: 5.2 Repurchase and reverse repurchase transactions
nodes.summary: The text outlines accounting treatment for repurchase (repos) and reverse repurchase (reverse repos) transactions. Repos, including those under LAF and MSF with RBI, are collateralized borrowings; securities remain in the investment account with coupon accrual, and borrowing costs are interest expense under Schedule 15. Reverse repos with RBI (up to 14 days, including LAF and SDF) are collateralized lending under Schedule 6; with banks/financial institutions (up to 14 days) under Schedule 7; revenue is interest income under Schedule 13. Reverse repos exceeding 14 days are collateralized lending under Schedule 9, with revenue as interest income under Schedule 13.

nodes.title: 5.3 Advances
nodes.summary: The text details the Bank's accounting policies for advances, covering classification into performing and non-performing advances (NPAs) per RBI guidelines, including netting adjustments. It explains transfers via inter-bank participation with and without risk. NPAs are sub-classified into sub-standard, doubtful, and loss assets, with provisions made at RBI-prescribed rates, though higher rates apply for schematic retail, agriculture, and Commercial Banking advances. Provisions for overseas branches follow host country regulations, and NCLT-referred NPAs are provisioned at the higher of RBI or resolution plan requirements. Fraud loans are fully provided as loss assets. Restructured assets are provisioned per RBI guidelines, with higher internal rates for COVID-19 and MSME restructurings. Write-offs and recoveries are recognized in the Profit and Loss Account. Appropriation of funds for standard advances follows specified orders. Additional provisions include those for defaulted accounts with resolution delays, non-cooperative/wilful defaulters, one-time settlements, Red Flagged Accounts, unhedged foreign currency exposure, incremental exposure beyond NPLL, general provisions on standard advances (higher for stressed sectors and certain ratings), group NPA provisions, non-funded outstanding provisions, home loan EMI waiver provisions, and a prudent provision of ₹5,012 crores for potential expected losses.

nodes.title: 5.4 Country risk
nodes.summary: The text outlines RBI guidelines for country risk provisioning on individual country exposures excluding the home country. Provisions apply only when net funded exposure exceeds 1% of total assets. Countries are classified into seven risk categories: insignificant, low, moderate, high, very high, restricted, and off-credit, based on internal parameters. For exposures over 180 days, provisions are graded from 0.25% to 100%; for exposures under 180 days, 25% of the normal requirement applies. No provision is held if exposure is below 1% of total assets. Indirect exposure is counted at 50%. These provisions are classified under Schedule 5 – Other Liabilities and Provisions.

nodes.title: 5.5 Securitisation and transfer of assets
nodes.summary: The text covers securitisation of standard assets, including loan sales via direct assignment or SPV, servicing, credit enhancement, accounting for gains/losses per AS-29 and RBI guidelines. It details transfer of loan exposures, accounting for realized profits/losses and amortization of premiums. Priority Sector Lending Certificates transactions are described, noting no loan asset transfer. Foreign currency translation for domestic operations and non-integral foreign branches is explained, including FCTR treatment. Finally, foreign exchange and derivative contracts are outlined, covering trading derivatives, revaluation methods, forward contracts, and currency futures mark-to-market procedures.

nodes.title: Loan Transfer, PSLC, and Foreign Currency Translation Guidelines
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting for transfer of loan exposures, including profit/loss recognition and amortization of premiums. It details Priority Sector Lending Certificates (PSLCs) transactions, noting no transfer of loan assets. It also explains translation of foreign currency items for domestic operations, including transaction date rates, closing rates for monetary assets/liabilities, and recognition of revaluation gains/losses. For non-integral foreign operations, it specifies translation of assets/liabilities at closing rates, income/expenses at transaction date rates, and accumulation of exchange differences in Foreign Currency Translation Reserve until disposal, with realized gains/losses recognized in Profit and Loss. Contingent liabilities in foreign currencies are disclosed at closing rates.

nodes.title: 5.8 Foreign exchange and derivative contracts
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting for foreign exchange and derivative contracts. It defines derivatives as forwards, swaps, FRAs, futures, and options, categorized as trading or hedging. Trading derivatives are revalued using market curves or FBIL rates, with unrealized gains/losses recognized in P&L and other assets/liabilities on a gross basis. Forward contracts are revalued at closing spot/forward rates or interpolated rates on a present value basis using ARR curves. Currency futures are marked-to-market daily using settlement prices, with daily settlement with the exchange. Exchange-traded currency options use internal models, and interest rate futures use exchange settlement prices. Option premiums are recognized on expiry or termination. Hedging derivatives, including funding swaps, are valued at closing spot, with premiums/discounts amortized. Hedge effectiveness is assessed, with fair value hedge changes in P&L and cash flow hedge effective portions in Cash Flow Hedge Reserve, recycled to P&L. Provisioning requires reversing receivables overdue over 90 days to a suspense account per RBI guidelines.

nodes.title: 5.9 Revenue recognition
nodes.summary: The text covers revenue recognition policies, including interest income accrual and exceptions for non-performing assets, amortization of discounts/premiums, and income from PTCs, guarantees, lockers, cards, and syndication fees. It details loan processing fees, penal charges, other fees, dividend income, and gain/loss on loan sell-downs. It also addresses PSLC fee amortization, RBI guidelines for non-performing advance sales, and bullion transactions. Additionally, it covers fixed assets and depreciation, including cost, capital work-in-progress, depreciation methods and useful lives, low-value asset depreciation, and disposal gains/losses. It includes impairment of fixed assets, non-banking assets, and operating lease transactions.

nodes.title: Fixed Assets, Impairment and Non-Banking Assets Accounting Policies
nodes.summary: The page covers bullion consignment and borrowing/lending accounting, fixed assets and depreciation (cost, capital work-in-progress, straight-line depreciation over estimated useful lives with a table comparing useful lives to Companies Act Schedule II, low-cost asset expensing, pro-rata depreciation on sales, disposal gains/losses, and Capital Reserve appropriation for premises sales), impairment of fixed assets (annual review, impairment loss recognition, recoverable amount as higher of net selling price and value in use with discounted cash flows, and revised depreciation), and non-banking assets acquired in satisfaction of claims, including land provisioning per RBI directions.

nodes.title: 5.13 Lease Transactions
nodes.summary:
5.13 Lease Transactions
Leases where the lessor effectively retains substantially all the risks and benefits of ownership over the lease term are classified as operating lease. Lease payments for assets taken on operating lease are recognised as an expense in the
355Financial statements
Profit and Loss Account on a straight-line basis over the lease term, unless the payments are structured to increase in line with expected general inflation to compensate for the lessor’s expected inflationary cost increase. Lease income from assets given on operating lease is recognized as income in the Profit and Loss Account on a straight line basis over the lease term.

nodes.title: 5.14 Employee benefits
nodes.summary: The text details employee benefits: short-term benefits (salaries/compensations recognized at undiscounted amounts in P&L). Defined benefit plans include provident fund (funded, actuarial valuation via Projected Unit Credit Method, actuarial gains/losses immediately recognized, overseas branches contribute to government schemes), gratuity (funded via insurers, actuarial valuation, gains/losses immediately recognized, provision for Code on Social Security 2020, overseas branches follow local laws), and resettlement allowance (unfunded, six months' pay for eligible Citibank acquisition employees, actuarial valuation). Defined contribution plans cover superannuation (10% of basic salary to LIC for regular employees; 15% to Superannuation Trust for Citibank acquisition employees with 10-year vesting) and National Pension Scheme (certain percentage of basic salary, managed by pension fund companies). All contributions recognized in P&L when accrued.

nodes.title: 5.15 Reward points
nodes.summary:
5.15 Reward points
The Bank runs a loyalty program which seeks to recognize and reward customers based on their relationship with the Bank. Under the program, eligible customers are granted loyalty points redeemable in future, subject to certain conditions. In addition, the Bank continues to grant reward points in respect of certain credit cards (not covered under the loyalty program). The Bank estimates the provision for such loyalty/reward points using an actuarial method at the Balance Sheet date through an independent actuary, basis assumptions such as redemption rate, lapse rate, discount rate, value of reward points etc. Provision for the said reward points is then made based on the actuarial valuation report as furnished by the said independent actuary.

nodes.title: 5.16 Taxation
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies: income tax including current and deferred tax, recognition and offsetting of deferred tax assets/liabilities, and reassessment; share issue expenses adjusted against share premium; corporate social responsibility expenditure recognition; earnings per share basic and diluted computation per AS-20; employee stock option/unit schemes including grant, fair value method, and accounting treatment; and provisions, contingent liabilities, and contingent assets recognition and disclosure per AS-29.

nodes.title: 5.17 Share issue expenses; 5.18 Corporate Social Responsibility
nodes.summary:
Financial statements
5.17 Share issue expenses
Share issue expenses are adjusted from the Share Premium Account in terms of Section 52 of the Companies Act, 2013.
5.18 Corporate Social Responsibility
Expenditure towards Corporate Social Responsibility is recognised in the Profit and Loss Account in accordance with the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013.

nodes.title: 5.19 Earnings per share
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies: earnings per share (basic/diluted per AS-20), employee stock option/unit schemes (grant terms, fair value method per RBI, accounting treatment), provisions and contingencies (recognition per AS-29, disclosure criteria, contingent assets), dividend accounting (not recognized as liability until payout per AS-4, but considered in capital adequacy), cash and cash equivalents definition, and segment reporting per AS-17 and RBI guidelines.

nodes.title: 1 Statutory disclosures as per RBI
nodes.summary: This section presents statutory disclosures as per RBI, covering regulatory capital composition (CET1, Tier 1, Tier 2, capital adequacy ratios, leverage ratio, and capital raised), capital and reserves movements (ESOPs, appropriations, investment reserve transition, AFS and cash flow hedge reserves), asset-liability management with maturity patterns, liquidity coverage ratio, and investment disclosures (HTM, AFS, FVTPL, subsidiary holdings). It details provisions for depreciation and Investment Fluctuation Reserve, Level 3 instrument gains/losses, HTM sales/transfers, non-SLR investment portfolio (NPAs and issuer composition), repo and GSL transactions, and asset quality (gross/net NPAs, sector-wise advances, overseas branches, resolution plans, restructuring, divergences, fraud provisions, COVID-19 resolution, capital market and country exposures, unsecured advances, intra-group exposures, unhedged foreign currency exposures, concentration of deposits and advances, derivatives, securitisation, customer complaints, RBI penalties, remuneration, business ratios, Bancassurance income, PSLC transactions, provisions and contingencies, Ind AS implementation, DICGC premium, non-banking assets, green deposits, other liabilities/assets, and expenses exceeding 1% of total income).

nodes.title: a) Composition of Regulatory Capital
nodes.summary: The text covers statutory disclosures as per RBI, focusing on regulatory capital under Basel III. It details the minimum capital ratio requirements (CET1, Tier 1, and total capital), and presents the Bank's capital adequacy ratios as of March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024, including CET1, Tier 1, Tier 2, total capital, risk-weighted assets, CRAR, leverage ratio, and the Government of India's shareholding percentage. It also lists the amounts of paid-up equity capital, non-equity Tier I, and Tier II capital raised during the year. Additionally, it notes equity capital raised through employee stock options, confirms no non-equity Tier I/Tier II capital was raised, and provides details of Tier II subordinated debt redeemed during the year, along with comparative prior-year information.

nodes.title: b) Capital and Reserves and Surplus
nodes.summary: The text covers the Bank's capital and reserves for FY2025 and FY2024, detailing share capital raised via employee stock options, no drawdown from reserves, appropriations to Capital Reserve (gain on HTM sale), Special Reserve under Income-tax Act, transition of Investment Reserve to General Reserve per RBI Investment Direction 2023, transfers to General Reserve from ESOP lapses and investment revaluation, Investment Fluctuation Reserve appropriation, AFS Reserve net appreciation, and Cash Flow Hedge Reserve loss. It also includes asset-liability management with maturity patterns of deposits, advances, investments, borrowings, and foreign currency assets/liabilities, plus qualitative and quantitative Liquidity Coverage Ratio disclosures across quarters. Finally, it presents investments disclosures: carrying value and fair value under HTM, AFS, FVTPL, and subsidiary/associate holdings, with provisions and composition for both years.

nodes.title: b) Movement of Provisions for Depreciation and Investment Fluctuation Reserve
nodes.summary: The text presents a financial table detailing the movement of provisions for depreciation on investments and the Investment Fluctuation Reserve (IFR) for March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024, in crores. Part A shows the opening balance, additions, transfers to General Reserve, write-offs/write-backs, and closing balance of depreciation provisions. Part B outlines the IFR's opening balance, transfers, drawdowns, and closing balance. Part C provides the closing IFR balance as a percentage of closing investments in AFS and FVTPL categories (net of provisions) and AFS and HFT categories (net of depreciation and non-performing investment provisions), with comparative percentages for both years.

nodes.title: d) Sale and transfers to/from HTM category
nodes.summary: The text details sales and transfers to/from the HTM category for the years ended 31 March 2025 and 2024. It states that these sales/transfers did not exceed 5% of the book value of HTM investments at the beginning of the year, excluding certain permitted transactions. It provides a table with particulars: opening carrying value of HTM securities (A), carrying value of all HTM securities sold during the year (B), less carrying values of securities sold under exempted situations (C), carrying value of securities sold (D=B-C), securities sold as a percentage of opening carrying value (E=D÷A), and the amount transferred to Capital Reserve for HTM securities sold at a gain.

nodes.title: e) Non-SLR investment portfolio
nodes.summary: The text details the non-SLR investment portfolio, including movement in non-performing non-SLR investments (opening balance, additions, reductions, closing balance, and provisions held) for March 31, 2025, and 2024. It also presents issuer composition of non-SLR investments as of both dates, covering total amounts, extent of private placement, and investments in unrated, unlisted, and below-grade securities, with a note that these categories are not mutually exclusive. The data excludes investments in non-SLR government securities.

nodes.title: f) Repo Transactions
nodes.summary: The section covers repo transactions, including securities sold/purchased under repos/reverse repos (LAF, MSF, Triparty, TLTRO) for years ended 31 March 2025 and 2024, with minimum, maximum, daily average, and year-end outstanding amounts in face and market value for government, corporate, and other securities, and notes no defaults in Term Reverse Repo settlements. It also covers Government Security Lending (GSL) transactions with outstanding and volume data, securities kept as margin with CCIL, RBI, NSCCIL, and ICCL, and begins Asset Quality disclosure with movement in gross non-performing assets. Additionally, it presents advances and NPA financial statements for March 31, 2025 and 2024, including gross NPA movement by category, provisions for NPAs, net NPA movement, classification of advances and provisions, footnotes on exchange rate impact, recoveries from NPA sales, technical write-offs, sale of NPAs, a provision for interest capitalization on restructured NPA accounts, reclassification of provision on moratorium loans, recoveries via Security Receipts, and key NPA ratios (gross NPA to gross advances, net NPA to net advances, provision coverage ratio, gross NPAs to gross customer assets, net NPAs to net customer assets).

nodes.title: f) Repo Transactions (intro)
nodes.summary: The text covers repo transactions, including securities sold/purchased under repos/reverse repos (including LAF, MSF, Triparty, and TLTRO) for years ended 31 March 2025 and 2024, with details on minimum, maximum, daily average, and year-end outstanding amounts in face and market value terms for government, corporate, and other securities, and notes no defaults in Term Reverse Repo settlements. It also covers Government Security Lending (GSL) transactions (market value) with outstanding and volume data for both years, securities kept as margin with CCIL, RBI, NSCCIL, and ICCL across various segments for both years, and the beginning of Asset Quality disclosure with movement in gross non-performing assets.

nodes.title: Advances
nodes.summary: The text presents financial statements detailing advances and non-performing assets (NPAs) for March 31, 2025 and 2024. It includes tables showing gross NPAs movement (opening balance, intra-category transfers, additions, reductions like upgradations, recoveries, and write-offs) and closing balances, categorized into standard, sub-standard, doubtful, and loss advances. It also covers movements in provisions for NPAs (opening balance, provisions made, exchange rate effects, transfers, write-offs/write-backs, closing balance) and net NPAs movement (opening balance, additions, reductions, floating provisions, interest capitalization). Additionally, it includes classification of advances and provisions held, with footnotes clarifying items like exchange rate impact, recoveries from NPA sales, and technical write-offs.

nodes.title: Advances
nodes.summary: The text presents financial figures including advances, provisions, and NPA ratios. It notes four points: sale of NPAs, a provision of ₹29.03 crores for interest capitalization on restructured NPA accounts not recognized as income per RBI guidelines, reclassification of ₹3,130.18 crores provision on moratorium loans from standard advances to other contingencies per COVID-19 regulatory package, and recoveries of ₹122.42 crores via Security Receipts. It also lists key NPA ratios for March 31, 2025 and 2024: gross NPA to gross advances, net NPA to net advances, provision coverage ratio, gross NPAs to gross customer assets, and net NPAs to net customer assets, with a note that customer assets include advances and credit substitutes.

nodes.title: b) Sector-wise advances
nodes.summary: The text presents sector-wise advances data for March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024, in crores. It covers priority sector advances including agriculture, industries eligible for priority sector lending, and services (banking, NBFCs, commercial real estate, trade), with sub-sectors like chemical products, basic metals, and infrastructure. It also covers personal loans (housing, vehicle loans). Similarly, it details non-priority sector advances for agriculture, industry, services, and personal loans. For each sector and sub-sector, it provides outstanding total advances, gross NPAs, and the percentage of gross NPAs to total advances for both years, along with notes on classification and italicized sub-sectors exceeding 10% of total outstanding advances.

nodes.title: d) Particulars of resolution plan and restructuring
nodes.summary: The text presents financial statement disclosures on resolution plans and restructuring for FY 2025 and FY 2024. It first details implementation of RBI's June 7, 2019 circular, showing the number of borrowers, outstanding amounts, and additional provisions for resolution plans not implemented within timelines versus those implemented during the year. It then provides a detailed table of accounts subjected to restructuring across four categories—agriculture, corporate (excluding MSME), MSME, and retail (excluding agriculture and MSME)—broken down by standard, sub-standard, doubtful, and loss assets, with borrower counts, gross amounts, and provisions held for both years, including footnotes on reporting scope and exclusions.

nodes.title: e) Divergence in asset classification and provisioning
nodes.summary: The text covers RBI-mandated disclosures on asset classification and provisioning divergences, noting no disclosure is required for FY2024 and FY2023 as thresholds were not met. It details loans not in default acquired and transferred during FY2025 and FY2024, including modes, principal outstanding, maturity, holding period, retention of economic interest, security coverage, and rating distribution. It states no agreements to replace transferred loans or pay damages. It provides details on stressed loans acquired (none) and transferred to ARCs and other entities, including accounts, principal, tenor, net book value, consideration, and provisions reversed. It also lists Security Receipts allotted and their recovery ratings as of March 31, 2025 and 2024.

nodes.title: g) Disclosure on provisioning pertaining to fraud accounts
nodes.summary: The text presents a table disclosing provisions for fraud accounts for the years ended 31 March 2025 and 2024, including number of frauds, amounts involved net of recoveries, provisions held at beginning and end, provisions made, balances in interest capitalisation accounts, and unamortised provisions debited from other reserves. It notes 17,281 digital payment fraud cases amounting to ₹124.35 crores in 2025 (previous year 32,068 cases, ₹158.96 crores), describes provisioning policy for advances versus other frauds, mentions 96 cases (₹7.13 crores) with claims not admitted, and excludes 316 written-off advance fraud cases (₹409.48 crores).

nodes.title: h) Disclosure under Resolution Framework for COVID-19-related Stress
nodes.summary: The text presents disclosures on COVID-19-related resolution frameworks, detailing movements in standard accounts for personal loans, corporate persons (including MSMEs), and others across H1/H2 FY24 and FY25, with exposures, NPAs, write-offs, and repayments in crores. It also covers exposures to the real estate sector (direct, indirect, and mortgage-backed securities) and capital market (direct investments, advances, stockbroker exposures, venture capital, etc.), risk category-wise country exposure with provisions, and unsecured advances including intangible securities, across March 2024 and March 2025.

nodes.title: Capital Market Exposure and Risk Category-wise Country Exposure
key_items: c) Details of Risk Category wise Country Exposure
nodes.summary: The page presents standalone financial statement excerpts covering two sections. Section b) details exposure to the capital market across ten categories, including direct equity investments, advances against securities, loans to stockbrokers, bridge loans, underwriting commitments, margin trading financing, and venture capital fund exposures, with amounts as of March 31, 2025 and 2024, and a total exposure figure. A footnote excludes certain restructuring-related equity conversions. Section c) provides risk category-wise country exposure, listing net exposure and provisions held as of March 31, 2025 and 2024 across risk categories from Insignificant to Restricted, with totals and a note on the internal risk categorization methodology.

nodes.title: d) Unsecured Advances
nodes.summary: The text covers unsecured advances of the bank as of March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024, including total amounts and nil intangible securities. It also details factoring exposures for both years. Additionally, it discloses intra-group exposures, including total and top-20 amounts, percentage of total exposure, and notes that exposures include credit, derivative, investment, and deposits for Priority Sector Lending shortfall. It confirms intra-group exposures were within RBI limits and certified by management and relied upon by auditors.

nodes.title: g) Unhedged foreign currency exposures
nodes.summary: This section covers the Bank's unhedged foreign currency exposure framework, including credit risk assessment, hedging requirements, monitoring, and RBI-compliant provisions and capital, with March 2025 and 2024 provision tables. It details concentration of deposits, advances, exposures, and NPAs for top twenty accounts, and derivative disclosures defining IRS, FRA, and CCS with outstanding notional principal, credit risk, fair values, risk management, accounting policies, and quantitative exposures for 2025 and 2024, noting no credit default swaps. Securitisation disclosures show no SPEs or securitised assets and detail transfers to the Depositor Education and Awareness Fund. Customer complaints data covers direct and Ombudsman complaints, disposal, awards, top-five grounds, and a summary. RBI penalties for FY 2024-25 and FY 2023-24 are listed with amounts, reasons, and payment dates. Remuneration disclosures include qualitative Nomination and Remuneration Committee and policy details and quantitative data for MD & CEO, Whole Time Directors, Material Risk Takers, and Non-executive Directors. Other disclosures cover business ratios, Bancassurance and marketing/distribution income, and PSLC purchases and sales with costs and fees, plus provisions and contingencies (income tax, NPAs, restructured assets, COVID-19/MSME restructuring, standard assets, unhedged foreign currency, country risk, resolution plan delays, legal cases, and others), and IFRS-converged Ind AS implementation status including RBI deferrals, diagnostic analysis, IT changes, proforma reporting, and oversight.

nodes.title: g) Unhedged foreign currency exposures (intro)
nodes.summary: This section covers the Bank's unhedged foreign currency exposure framework, including credit risk assessment, hedging requirements, monitoring, and provisions/capital per RBI guidelines, with a table of provisions for March 2025 and 2024. It also details concentration of deposits, advances, exposures, and NPAs for top twenty accounts. Derivative disclosures define IRS, FRA, and CCS, and provide outstanding notional principal, credit risk, fair values, risk management structure, accounting policies, and quantitative exposures for 2025 and 2024, noting no credit default swaps. Securitisation disclosures show no SPEs or securitised assets, and detail transfers to the Depositor Education and Awareness Fund. Customer complaints data includes complaints received directly and via Ombudsman, disposal, awards, top-five grounds, and overall summary. RBI penalties levied in FY 2024-25 and FY 2023-24 are listed with amounts, reasons, and payment dates. Remuneration disclosures include qualitative details on the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, policy features, and quantitative data for MD & CEO, Whole Time Directors, Material Risk Takers, and Non-executive Directors. Other disclosures present business ratios, Bancassurance and marketing/distribution income, and Priority Sector Lending Certificates purchased.

nodes.title: 1.6 Concentration of deposits, advances, exposures and NPAs
nodes.summary: The text details the Bank's framework for managing credit risk from unhedged foreign currency exposures, including assessment factors, hedging requirements based on internal ratings, policy applicability, monitoring, and additional provisions/capital per RBI guidelines. It provides a table showing provisions for unhedged exposures for March 31, 2025 and 2024, covering opening provision, acquisition transfer, release, cumulative provision, and incremental capital. Additionally, it presents concentration data for deposits, advances, exposures, and NPAs, with amounts and percentages for the top twenty depositors, borrowers, exposures, and NPA accounts as of both dates, including footnotes defining advances and exposures.

nodes.title: 1.7 Derivatives
nodes.summary: This section details the bank's derivative disclosures. It defines Interest Rate Swaps (IRS), Forward Rate Agreements (FRA), and Cross Currency Swaps (CCS), and provides outstanding notional principal, potential losses, collateral, credit risk concentration, and fair values for 2025 and 2024. It lists nature and terms of IRS, FRA, and CCS, including benchmarks. It covers exchange-traded interest rate derivatives, disclosing notional amounts undertaken and outstanding. It outlines qualitative risk management structure, accounting policies for hedging and trading derivatives, provisioning and collateral, and quantitative risk exposure including notional principal, mark-to-market positions, credit exposure, and PV01 for 2025 and 2024. It also discloses outstanding exchange-traded interest rate futures and currency options, and states no Credit Default Swaps were undertaken.

nodes.title: 1.8 Disclosures relating to securitisation
nodes.summary: The text covers securitisation disclosures under RBI guidelines, showing no SPEs, securitised assets, retained exposures, or sale consideration for 2025 and 2024. It states the Bank has no consolidated special purpose vehicle. It details transfers to the Depositor Education and Awareness Fund, including opening balances, additions, reimbursements, and closing balances for both years. Customer complaints are summarized with numbers received, disposed, rejected, and pending for the Bank and Ombudsman, including award implementation status. An overall complaints summary shows total complaints, those redressed within one working day, and net reportable complaints for both financial years.

nodes.title: 1.11 Disclosure of customer complaints
nodes.summary: The text presents customer complaint disclosures for FY 2024-25 and 2023-24, including a summary of complaints received directly and via the Office of Ombudsman (OBO), with counts of pending, received, disposed, rejected, and resolved complaints, awards, and unimplemented awards. It provides an overall complaints summary (total, redressed within one working day, net reportable) and a top-five grounds breakdown (credit cards, account opening/operation, ATM/debit cards, internet/mobile banking, loans) with pending, received, percentage change, end-of-year pending, and pending beyond 30 days. A note clarifies that redressed-in-one-day complaints are excluded and certified by Management and relied upon by auditors.

nodes.title: 1.12 Details of penalty/stricture levied by RBI
nodes.summary: The text details RBI penalties levied during FY 2024-25 and FY 2023-24. For FY 2024-25, it lists a penalty of ₹1.91 crores paid on 12 September 2024 for non-compliance with Section 19(1)(a) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, and RBI directions on Interest Rate on Deposits, KYC, and collateral-free agricultural loans. For FY 2023-24, it lists two penalties: ₹0.30 crores paid on 27 June 2023 for non-compliance with RBI directions on Prudential Norms for Credit Card Accounts, and ₹0.91 crores paid on 17 November 2023 for non-compliance with KYC Directions 2016, Loans and Advances restrictions, outsourcing risk guidelines, and current account conduct rules. Each entry includes amount, reason, and payment date.

nodes.title: 1.13 Disclosure on Remuneration
nodes.summary: The section covers disclosure on remuneration. Qualitative disclosures detail the Nomination and Remuneration Committee's composition, mandate, and objectives; use of external consultants; scope of policy (domestic and overseas branches); employee categories; compensation philosophy and key features (affordability, pay for performance, variable pay, ESOPs/ESUs); alignment with RBI guidelines; policy review; independent remuneration for risk, audit, and compliance staff; risk consideration via Balanced Scorecard; performance linkage; adjustment measures for weak performance; deferral and vesting policies; malus and clawback; and forms of variable remuneration with rationale. Quantitative disclosures present remuneration data for MD & CEO, Whole Time Directors, Material Risk Takers, and Non-executive Directors for FY2025 and FY2024, including committee meetings and sitting fees; number of employees receiving variable awards; sign-on bonuses; severance pay; outstanding deferred remuneration; breakdown of fixed and variable pay; ex post adjustments; number of MRTs; malus and clawback cases; mean pay and deviation for WTDs; and fixed remuneration for Non-executive Directors.

nodes.title: Qualitative disclosures
nodes.summary: The text covers the disclosure on remuneration, detailing the Nomination and Remuneration Committee's composition, mandate, and objectives. It describes the use of external consultants for benchmarking, the scope of the remuneration policy (domestic and overseas branches, not subsidiaries), and employee categories covered. It outlines the compensation philosophy, key features (affordability, pay for performance, variable pay, ESOPs/ESUs), alignment with RBI guidelines, and policy review. It explains how risk, internal audit, and compliance employees are remunerated independently, how current and future risks are considered via Balanced Scorecard, performance linkage, and measures to adjust remuneration for weak performance. It details deferral and vesting policies, malus and clawback arrangements, and forms of variable remuneration (variable pay, ESOPs, ESUs) with rationale and factors determining mix.

nodes.title: Quantitative disclosures
nodes.summary: The text presents quantitative disclosures on remuneration for the MD & CEO, Whole Time Directors, Material Risk Takers (MRTs), and Non-executive Directors for FY2025 and FY2024. It covers Remuneration Committee meetings and sitting fees; number of employees receiving variable awards; sign-on/joining bonuses in stock options, fair value, and cash; severance pay; outstanding deferred remuneration in cash and shares; deferred remuneration paid out in cash and vested stock options; breakdown of fixed and variable pay, deferred and non-deferred components, and forms (cash vs. share-linked); outstanding deferred and retained remuneration subject to ex post adjustments; reductions due to explicit and implicit adjustments; number of MRTs; cases of malus and clawback; mean pay and deviation for WTDs; and fixed remuneration for Non-executive Directors.

nodes.title: 1.14 Other Disclosures
nodes.summary: The text presents 'Other Disclosures' with business ratios for March 2025 and 2024, including interest income, non-interest income, cost of deposits, net interest margin, operating profit, return on assets, business per employee, and profit per employee, with footnotes defining working funds, net interest income, operating profit, and productivity ratios. It also covers Bancassurance business income from life and non-life insurance policies, Marketing and Distribution business income from mutual funds, alternate products, government bonds, publicity material display fees, and others, and begins a disclosure on Priority Sector Lending Certificates (PSLCs) purchased/sold, specifically detailing PSLCs purchased by the Bank.

nodes.title: Category
nodes.summary: The text presents financial data on PSLC purchases and sales for 2025 and 2024, including costs and fees. It details provisions and contingencies, such as income tax, non-performing assets, restructured assets, COVID-19/MSME restructuring, standard assets, unhedged foreign currency, country risk, resolution plan delays, legal cases, and other contingencies, with notes on non-performing advances and investments. It also covers the status of IFRS-converged Ind AS implementation, including RBI deferrals, diagnostic analysis, IT system changes, proforma reporting, and oversight by a Steering Committee, Audit Committee, and Board.

nodes.title: g) Payment of DICGC Insurance Premium
nodes.summary: The text presents financial disclosures: DICGC insurance premium payments and arrears for March 2025 and 2024; land provisions under non-banking assets with amounts, provisions, and reversals; a statement that no letters of comfort were issued; portfolio-level green deposit fund usage with categories and unallocated amounts (all nil); details of 'Others' in other liabilities (mark-to-market forex/derivative liability exceeding 1% of total assets in 2025) and other assets (mark-to-market assets and priority sector shortfall deposits exceeding 1% in respective years); confirmation that no miscellaneous income item exceeded 1% of total income; and expenses exceeding 1% of total income, listing commission to DSAs, network partner charges, cashback, professional fees, business promotion, and priority sector lending certificate charges with amounts for both years.

nodes.title: 2. Other Disclosures
nodes.summary: The section covers EPS computation, employee stock option schemes, proposed dividends, segmental reporting, and related party disclosures. It includes geographic segment data, related party classifications, subsidiary and step-down subsidiary lists, associate transactions, lease and fixed asset movements, deferred tax, employee benefit plans, provisions, MSMED disclosures, and CSR spend. Contingent liabilities include unspent CSR, claims, partly paid investments, forward exchange contracts, derivative contracts, guarantees, acceptances, endorsements, rediscounted bills, capital contracts, and other commitments. The auditor's opinion on consolidated financial statements covers compliance, key audit matters (IT systems, IRAC), internal financial controls, and includes the consolidated profit and loss account, cash flow statement, and balance sheet schedules.

nodes.title: 2. Other Disclosures (intro)
nodes.summary: The section covers other disclosures: EPS computation for 2025 and 2024, including basic/diluted earnings, weighted average shares, and stock option dilution; employee stock option/unit schemes, with grant data, activity tables, fair value methodology (Black-Scholes), compensation costs, and valuation assumptions; proposed dividend not recognized as liability, and prior year dividend paid; segmental reporting by business segments (Treasury, Retail Banking, Corporate/Wholesale Banking, Other Banking) and geographic segments (domestic/international), with financial data; and related party disclosures categorizing promoters, key management personnel, relatives, and subsidiaries.

nodes.title: 2.1 Earnings Per Share (‘EPS’)
nodes.summary: The text covers 'Other Disclosures' with a focus on Earnings Per Share (EPS) computation for the years ended 31 March 2025 and 2024. It presents basic and diluted earnings (net profit after tax) in crores, basic and diluted weighted average number of shares, and the adjustment for equity shares from stock options/units under ESOP/ESU schemes. It details basic EPS, the effect of potential equity shares, diluted EPS, and nominal value of shares. The dilution is attributed to 18,432,380 stock options/units (previous year 22,287,930). The data is part of the Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 standalone financial statements.

nodes.title: 2.2 Employee Stock Options/Units
nodes.summary: The text details employee stock option and unit schemes of a bank, including approvals for up to 315,087,000 options and 50,000,000 units vesting over 3-4 years and 3 years respectively, exercisable within five years. It provides grant data for the year ended 31 March 2025, including dates, prices, and numbers, along with stock option and unit activity tables for both 2025 and 2024 (outstanding, granted, forfeited, expired, exercised, exercisable). It covers fair value methodology using the Black-Scholes model per RBI guidelines, compensation costs recognized and recovered, and valuation assumptions such as dividend yield, expected life, risk-free rate, and volatility. Weighted average fair values of grants are also stated.

nodes.title: 2.3 Proposed Dividend
nodes.summary:
2.3 Proposed Dividend
The Board of Directors, in their meeting held on 24 April, 2025 have proposed a final dividend of `1 per equity share amounting to `309.74 crores. The proposal is subject to the approval of shareholders at the Annual General Meeting. In terms of revised Accounting Standard (AS) 4 ‘Contingencies and Events occurring after the Balance sheet date’ as notified by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs through the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, 2021, such proposed dividend has not been recognised as a liability as on 31 March, 2025.
During the year, the Bank paid final dividend of `1 per equity share amounting `309.09 crores pertaining to the previous year ended 31 March, 2024.

nodes.title: 2.4 Segmental reporting
nodes.summary: The text details segmental reporting for a bank, dividing business into Treasury, Retail Banking (including Digital Banking as a sub-segment), Corporate/Wholesale Banking, and Other Banking Business, per RBI guidelines. It outlines each segment's principal activities, revenue sources, and expense components, including inter-segment transfers and allocation methodologies. Unallocated assets and liabilities are also covered. The text provides extensive financial data for the years ended 31 March 2025 and 2024, including segment revenue, results, assets, liabilities, capital expenditure, and depreciation. Additionally, it presents geographic segment information for domestic and international operations, covering revenue, assets, capital expenditure, and depreciation.

nodes.title: 2.5 Related party disclosure
nodes.summary: The text outlines the Bank's related party disclosures, categorizing related parties into Promoters (SUUTI until July 17, 2023, and LIC), Key Management Personnel (Amitabh Chaudhry, Rajiv Anand, Subrat Mohanty, Munish Sharda with their effective dates), Relatives of Key Management Personnel (a list of 29 individuals), and Subsidiary Companies (including Axis Capital, Axis Trustee, Axis Asset Management, Axis Mutual Fund Trustee, Axis UK, Axis Finance, Axis Securities, A.Treds, Freecharge entities, with an effective date for one). It includes numerical figures but no context, and a page number 415.

nodes.title: Geographic Segments and Related Party Disclosures
key_items: c) Relatives of Key Management Personnel
nodes.summary: The page presents standalone financial statements with geographic segment data for domestic and international operations, showing revenue, assets, capital expenditure, and depreciation for the years ended 31 March 2025 and 2024 (in crores). It includes a note on related party disclosures classifying related parties into promoters, key management personnel, and their relatives. Promoters include the Administrator of SUUTI (up to 17 July 2023) and LIC. Key management personnel are Amitabh Chaudhry, Rajiv Anand, Subrat Mohanty, and Munish Sharda, with effective dates for the latter two. Relatives of key management personnel are listed by name, covering family members of the executives.

nodes.title: f) Associate
nodes.summary: The Associate section covers related party disclosures for Axis Bank for FY2025 and FY2024, including transactions with promoters, key management personnel, relatives, subsidiaries, and step-down subsidiaries, detailing dividends, interest, investments, remuneration, services, foreign exchange, and balances payable/receivable. It also presents lease disclosures for operating leases, movement in fixed assets capitalized as software and intangibles, deferred tax assets and liabilities from timing differences, and employee benefit plans such as provident fund, superannuation, national pension scheme, gratuity, resettlement allowance, and a provision for the Code of Social Security 2020. Additionally, it includes provisions and contingencies, MSMED Act disclosures for delayed payments, and Corporate Social Responsibility spend and accruals for FY2024-25 and FY2023-24.

nodes.title: f) Associate (intro)
nodes.summary: The text presents related party disclosures for Axis Bank for FY2025 and FY2024, including transactions with promoters, key management personnel, relatives, subsidiaries, and step-down subsidiaries, with details on items like dividends, interest, investments, remuneration, services, and foreign exchange. It also provides balances payable/receivable and maximum balances during the year. Additionally, it covers lease disclosures for assets taken and given on operating lease, movement in fixed assets capitalised as application software and intangibles, components of deferred tax assets and liabilities, and employee benefits related to the provident fund, including actuarial valuation of any deficiency.

nodes.title: Deferred tax assets
nodes.summary: The section covers deferred tax assets and liabilities from timing differences, including provisions for loan losses, employee benefits, FCTR, depreciation, special reserve, MTM transition gain, and interest on income tax refund, with net deferred tax assets. It details various employee benefit plans: Provident Fund (interest deficiency, actuarial valuation, financial components, assumptions), Superannuation and National Pension Scheme contributions, Gratuity (financials, experience adjustments, assumptions), and Resettlement allowance provision. It also includes a provision for the probable impact of the Code of Social Security 2020, provisions and contingencies (frauds, reward points, other contingencies with movements and components), disclosures under the MSMED Act for delayed payments to micro and small enterprises, and Corporate Social Responsibility activities, required spend, expenditure, and accruals for FY 2024-25 and FY 2023-24.

nodes.title: 2.9 Employee Benefits
nodes.summary: The text covers financial statement notes: movement in fixed assets capitalized as application software and intangibles/goodwill, showing cost, additions, deductions, accumulated depreciation/amortization, closing balances, and depreciation/amortization charges for 2025 and 2024, including exchange rate fluctuations. It also details major components of deferred tax assets and liabilities from timing differences, listing specific items such as provisions for loan losses, employee benefits, FCTR, depreciation, special reserve, MTM transition gain, and interest on income tax refund, with net deferred tax assets. Finally, it begins a section on employee benefits.

nodes.title: Provident Fund
nodes.summary: The text covers the Bank's Provident Fund rules, stating that any interest deficiency below the government-declared rate must be made good by the Bank; an actuarial valuation found no deficiency. It presents Profit and Loss and Balance Sheet components for the Provident Fund benefit plan, including net employee benefit expenses, fair value of plan assets, present value of obligations, and changes in defined benefit obligation and plan assets. Experience adjustments and major plan asset categories are detailed, along with principal actuarial assumptions. Contributions to the Employee Pension Scheme, Superannuation plan (including a separate scheme for former Citibank employees), National Pension Scheme, and Gratuity plan components are also summarized.

nodes.title: Employee Benefit Plans: Financials, Assumptions, Superannuation, and NPS
nodes.summary: The page provides financial statement data on defined benefit plans, including fair value of plan assets, defined benefit obligations, surplus/deficit, experience adjustments, and movements in plan assets across March 2025 to 2021. It details major asset categories (government securities, debt, equity, others) and principal actuarial assumptions (discount rates, expected returns). It also covers contributions to the employee provident fund and pension scheme, superannuation plan contributions and accruals for Citibank-acquired employees under a separate defined contribution scheme, and National Pension Scheme contributions for opting employees.

nodes.title: Gratuity
nodes.summary: This text presents gratuity benefit plan financials, including net employee benefit expenses and balance sheet recognition. It details changes in defined benefit obligations and plan assets, experience adjustments over five years, and major plan asset categories (government securities, bonds, equity, etc.). Principal actuarial assumptions are provided: discount rate, expected return on plan assets, salary escalation, and employee turnover by age. Notes explain salary increase estimates and expected return basis, and state that future contributions are not determinable. The information is actuary-certified and relied upon by auditors.

nodes.title: Resettlement allowance
nodes.summary: The text covers a resettlement allowance provision of ₹0.21 crores for the year ended 31 March 2025, based on actuarial valuation. It includes balance sheet figures for current and non-current liabilities for 2025 and 2024, net liability under Schedule 5, and principal actuarial assumptions such as discount rate, salary escalation rate, and employee turnover rates by age group.

nodes.title: Provision towards probable impact on account of Code of Social Security 2020
nodes.summary:
Provision towards probable impact on account of Code of Social Security 2020
The Bank on a prudent basis as per internal policy, based on an actuarial valuation holds a provision of `367.85 crores as on 31 March 2025 (`287.60 crores as on 31 March, 2024) towards the gratuity liability on account of probable impact due to Code of Social Security 2020. This is over and above the provisions made in normal course based on extant rules and as reported in the above disclosure.
The above information is as certified by the actuary and relied upon by the auditors.

nodes.title: 2.10 Provisions and contingencies
nodes.summary: The text presents provisions and contingencies, detailing movements in crore for three categories as of March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024. It covers the provision for frauds under other liabilities with opening balance, additions, reductions, and closing balance. It includes the provision for reward points on an actuarial basis, showing opening provision, provision made, reductions, and closing provision. It also details the provision for other contingencies with opening provision, reclassification from provision on standard advances, additions, reductions, and closing provision. Notes explain the reclassification of COVID-19 provision to other contingencies, additions including exchange rate fluctuation, and components of the closing provision such as legal cases, resolution plan delays, AIF investments, and future expected losses. Comparative figures for both years are provided.

nodes.title: 2.11 Small and Micro Enterprises
nodes.summary: The text outlines disclosures required under the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006, effective from 2 October 2006, regarding delayed payments to MSMED-registered vendors. It lists particulars: principal and interest unpaid, interest paid under Section 16 with payments beyond due dates, interest due for delayed payments without MSMED interest, interest accrued and unpaid, and further interest due in succeeding years until paid, disallowed as deductible expenditure under Section 23. It provides comparative figures as of 31 March 2025 and 31 March 2024 for principal and interest, with a footnote for amounts less than ₹50,000, and states the information is based on bank records relied upon by auditors.

nodes.title: 2.12 Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)
nodes.summary: The text details the Bank's Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) for FY 2024-25 and FY 2023-24. It states the required CSR spend: ₹425.92 crores (previous year ₹267.15 crores). It lists CSR activities across seven areas: Lives & Livelihoods, Financial Literacy & Financial Inclusion, Education, Environmental Sustainability, Humanitarian & Relief, Health & Nutrition, and Sports. For both years, it provides amounts required, expenditure incurred, and accruals for unspent obligations. It also reports CSR expense recognized in profit and loss: ₹426.57 crores (previous year ₹268.66 crores), broken down into cash and provisions (yet to be paid). A footnote notes transfer to an unspent CSR account for ongoing projects.

nodes.title: c) Movement in the provision towards unspent CSR amount
nodes.summary: The text details movement in the provision for unspent CSR amounts for the years ended 31 March 2025 and 2024, including opening balances, additions, reductions, and closing balances. It also includes disclosures per Ministry of Corporate Affairs notification dated 24 March 2021, stating the Bank has not granted advances/loans/investments or guarantees with an understanding to further lend, nor received funds with such understanding. Finally, it describes contingent liabilities: claims against the Bank not acknowledged as debts (with provision amounts), liability for partly paid investments, and liability on account of forward exchange contracts (including NDF contracts and notional principal).

nodes.title: d) Liability on account of derivative contracts
nodes.summary: The text covers contingent liabilities in a bank's financial statements: derivative contracts (currency options/swaps, exchange-traded options, non-deliverable derivatives, interest/currency futures, forward rate agreements) with definitions and notional principal as contingent liability; guarantees for constituents, net of cash margin; acceptances, endorsements, and documentary credits, net of cash margin; other contingent items like bills rediscounted, capital contracts, Tom/Spot FX contracts, investment purchase contracts, indemnity deed, resolution plan undertakings, IPO commitments, associate investment, and DEAF transfers. It also notes periodic assessment for foreseeable losses on long-term contracts with adequate provisions, and prior-year figure regrouping. Signatures of auditors and directors are included.

nodes.title: Financial Derivatives and Contingent Liabilities Overview
key_items: e) Guarantees given on behalf of constituents
f) Acceptances, endorsements and other obligations
nodes.summary: The text covers financial derivatives including currency options, non-deliverable options, and currency futures, explaining their features and contingent liability as notional principal. It describes the Bank's off-setting inter-bank transactions leading to higher gross notional principal but lower net market risk. It also details guarantees given on behalf of constituents to enhance credit standing, stating they are irrevocable assurances net of cash margin in Schedule 12 – Contingent Liabilities. Finally, it covers acceptances, endorsements, and other obligations such as documentary credits and accepted or endorsed bills, also net of cash margin in Schedule 12.

nodes.title: g) Other items for which the Bank is contingently liable
nodes.summary: The text covers the Bank's contingent liabilities and other items, including rediscounted bills, capital contracts, foreign exchange contracts, investment purchase contracts, indemnity deeds, resolution plan undertakings, IPO commitments, associate investments, and DEAF transfers. It describes the Bank's process for assessing long-term contracts for foreseeable losses, with provisions recorded and disclosed. It notes prior-year figure reclassification, includes auditor signatures from M M Nissim & Co LLP and KKC & Associates LLP, and lists Axis Bank's board, CEO, CFO, and Company Secretary. It also references the Independent Auditor's Report to members on consolidated financial statements.

nodes.title: Opinion
nodes.summary: The section presents the auditor's opinion on Axis Bank's consolidated financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2025, covering the balance sheet, profit and loss account, cash flow statement, and notes, with assertions of compliance with the Banking Regulation Act, Companies Act, RBI guidelines, and Accounting Standards, and a true and fair view. It outlines the basis for opinion, including auditing standards and ethical requirements. Key audit matters include Information Technology systems and controls over financial reporting, with procedures to assess IT risks and controls. It also addresses Income Recognition, Asset Classification, and Provisioning (IRAC) on advances for Axis Securities Limited and Axis Finance Limited, covering regulatory requirements, loan figures, provisioning, RBI guidelines, and audit procedures for NPAs, along with IT risks, audit approaches, testing of IT controls, audit opinions, management and auditor responsibilities, other information review, and legal and regulatory compliance.

nodes.title: Opinion (intro)

nodes.title: a. Investments classified under the HTM category
nodes.summary:
a. Investments classified under the HTM category
Investments held in HTM category are carried at cost and are not Mark-to-Market (‘MTM’) after initial recognition. Any discount or premium on the investments under HTM category is amortised over the remaining life of the instrument. The amortised amount is reflected under item II ‘Income on Investments’ of Schedule 13: ‘Interest Earned’ with a contra in Schedule 8: ‘Investments’.
Realised gains on sale of investments in HTM category are recognised in the Profit and Loss Account and subsequently appropriated to the Capital Reserve Account (net of taxes and transfer to statutory reserves) in accordance with the RBI guidelines. Realised losses are recognised in the Profit and Loss Account.

nodes.title: b. Investments classified under AFS category
nodes.summary: The text outlines accounting for Available-for-Sale (AFS) investments: fair valuation, amortization of discount/premium on debt securities with corresponding entries in interest income and investments, aggregation of net valuation gains/losses (net of tax) directly to AFS Reserve without P&L, AFS Reserve as CET1 capital but not for dividend/coupon distribution, transfer of accumulated gains/losses to P&L on sale/maturity of debt instruments, and for designated equity instruments, gains/losses on sale transferred from AFS Reserve to Capital Reserve per RBI Investment Direction, 2023.

nodes.title: c. Investments classified under FVTPL category
nodes.summary:
c. Investments classified under FVTPL category
Investments held under FVTPL category are fair valued and the net gain or loss arising on such valuation is directly credited or debited to the Profit and Loss Account.
Any discount or premium on the debt securities under FVTPL category is amortised over the remaining life of the instrument. The amortised amount is reflected in the financial statements under item II ‘Income on Investments’ of Schedule 13: ‘Interest Earned’ with a contra in Schedule 8: ‘Investments’.

nodes.title: d. Investments in Subsidiaries, Associates and Joint Ventures

It also covers employee benefits: Provident Fund disclosures for Axis Bank and its Group, including contributions, obligations, benefit expenses, funded status, and actuarial assumptions; Superannuation contributions and accrual for Citibank-acquired employees; National Pension Scheme contributions; Leave Encashment liabilities for group companies with actuarial assumptions; and Gratuity plan details including net benefit expenses, funded status, balance sheet provisions, changes in obligations and plan assets, experience adjustments, asset categories, and actuarial assumptions for the company and its subsidiaries.

nodes.title: As at (intro)
nodes.summary: The text presents a comparative financial statement of deferred tax assets and liabilities as of 31 March 2025 and 31 March 2024. It lists deferred tax assets from provisions for loan losses/doubtful debts, employee benefits, Foreign Currency Translation Reserve, and other items, totaling 6,120.10 and 5,917.32 respectively. Deferred tax liabilities include depreciation on fixed assets, Special Reserve under the Income Tax Act, transition gain on mark-to-market investments, interest on income tax refund, and other items, totaling 1,302.70 and 685.13. The net deferred tax asset is 4,614.62 and 5,434.97. The text also references Schedule 2 (V)(A) of the Consolidated Balance Sheet and is labeled as part of financial statements (page 487).
