nodes.title: Provident Fund
nodes.summary: The text details the Provident Fund disclosures for Axis Bank and its Group, including contributions of ₹460.67 crores for FY2025 (previous year ₹408.92 crores). It outlines the Bank's obligation to cover any interest deficiency in the Trust, with no deficiency found via actuarial valuation. It presents tables summarizing net benefit expenses, funded status, and balance sheet recognition, including changes in defined benefit obligations and plan assets, experience adjustments, and major asset categories (government securities, debt, equity, others). Principal actuarial assumptions such as discount rates, expected returns, and guaranteed rates are also provided.

nodes.title: Superannuation
nodes.summary: The text covers employee benefit plans: Superannuation contributions by the Group (₹15.07 crores) and accrual for Citibank-acquired employees (₹12.93 crores); National Pension Scheme contributions (₹22.22 crores); Leave Encashment liability based on actuarial valuation for Axis Capital, Freecharge, and A.Treds, with assumptions on salary escalation and discount rates for 2025 and 2024; and Gratuity plan details including net benefit expenses, actual return on plan assets, and balance sheet provisions showing present values of obligations, fair value of plan assets, and net liability/asset positions for 2025 and 2024.

nodes.title: Group Financials: NPS Contributions and Leave Encashment Liabilities
nodes.summary: This page presents financial statement disclosures for the Group. It covers the National Pension Scheme (NPS), detailing contributions of ₹22.22 crores (previous year ₹15.54 crores) for opted employees. It also covers Leave Encashment, reporting actuarial valuations of privilege leave liabilities for Axis Capital Ltd., Freecharge Payment Technologies Pvt. Ltd., and A.Treds Ltd. as of March 31, 2025 and 2024. The associated total expenses under Schedule 16(I) and actuarial assumptions—salary escalation rate and discount rate—are provided for both years.

nodes.title: Gratuity
nodes.summary: The text presents gratuity benefit plan disclosures, including tables of net benefit expenses in the Profit and Loss Account and funded status in the Balance Sheet for 2025 and 2024. It details components of employee benefit expense, actual return on plan assets, and balance sheet provisions for funded and unfunded obligations. Changes in defined benefit obligation and fair value of plan assets are shown, along with experience adjustments from 2021 to 2025. Major plan asset categories (managed by insurers) and principal actuarial assumptions (discount rate, expected return, salary escalation, employee turnover) are provided for the company and its subsidiaries: Axis Capital Ltd., Axis Asset Management Company Ltd., Axis Securities Ltd., Axis Finance Ltd., and Axis Trustee Services Ltd.

nodes.title: A. Treds Ltd.
nodes.summary: This section on A. Treds Ltd. presents actuarial assumptions and plan asset details (discount rates, expected returns, salary escalation, employee turnover) for A. Treds Ltd., Freecharge Payment Technologies, and Axis Pension Fund Management for 2025 and 2024. It discloses a resettlement allowance provision of ₹0.21 crores, net liability figures under Schedule 5, and an actuarial provision of ₹385.05 crores for the Code of Social Security 2020, note that expected plan contributions are not determinable, all actuary-certified and auditor-relied upon. It covers MSMED Act disclosures on delayed payments to micro and small enterprises, provisions and contingencies movements (frauds, reward points, COVID-19 reclassification), Ministry of Corporate Affairs notification compliance on lending/guarantee arrangements, expenses exceeding 1% of total income, and Schedule III additional information on net assets and profit/loss of the parent, subsidiaries, step-down subsidiaries, minority interest, and associates. It also details contingent liabilities from disputed claims and tax demands (₹904.76 crores provision), partly paid investments, forward exchange and derivative contracts, guarantees, and acceptances/endorsements.

nodes.title: A. Treds Ltd. (intro)
nodes.summary: The text covers actuarial assumptions and plan asset details for A.Treds Ltd., Freecharge Payment Technologies, and Axis Pension Fund Management for 2025 and 2024, including discount rates, expected returns, salary escalation, and employee turnover. It also details a resettlement allowance provision of ₹0.21 crores, net liability figures, and a provision of ₹385.05 crores for the Code of Social Security 2020. Additionally, it includes MSMED Act disclosures on delayed payments to micro and small enterprises, with principal and interest amounts for 2025 and 2024, and notes actuarial certification and auditor reliance.

nodes.title: Financial Statements: Resettlement Allowance and Social Security Provision
key_items: Provision towards probable impact on account of Code of Social Security 2020
nodes.summary: The text presents financial statement disclosures on two actuarial provisions. It first notes that the expected plan contribution for the next annual period is not determinable due to various internal/external factors, as certified by the actuary and relied upon by auditors. For resettlement allowance, the Profit and Loss account shows a provision of ₹0.21 crores for the year ended 31 March 2025 (previous year Nil) based on independent actuarial valuation, with Balance Sheet current and non-current liabilities, net liability under Schedule 5, and actuarial assumptions (discount rate, salary escalation, employee turnover by age groups). For the Code of Social Security 2020, a prudent internal-policy provision of ₹385.05 crores as on 31 March 2025 (₹287.60 crores as on 31 March 2024) is held for probable gratuity liability impact, over and above normal provisions, also actuary-certified and auditor-reiled upon.

nodes.title: 1.13 Small and Micro Enterprises
nodes.summary: The text addresses compliance with the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006, requiring disclosures on delayed payments to MSMED-registered vendors. It presents data for Axis Bank Ltd. and its subsidiaries/group, covering principal and interest amounts unpaid, interest paid under Section 16, interest due for delays, accrued unpaid interest, and further interest payable in subsequent years (disallowed as deductible expenditure under Section 23). Figures are provided for 31 March 2025 and 31 March 2024 in crores, with notes on amounts below ₹50,000 and reliance on group information by auditors.

nodes.title: 1.14 Provisions and contingencies
nodes.summary: The text covers three main sections: (1.14) Provisions and contingencies, detailing movements in provisions for frauds, reward points, and other contingencies, including a reclassification of COVID-19 provisions; (1.15) Disclosure under Ministry of Corporate Affairs notification regarding transactions not involving further lending or guarantee arrangements; (1.16) Expenses exceeding 1% of total income, listing items like commissions, network charges, cashback, and professional fees for 2025 and 2024; and (1.17) Additional information under Schedule III of the Companies Act, 2013, providing net assets and profit/loss contributions of the parent and subsidiaries.

nodes.title: Financial Statements Disclosures on Regulated Transactions and Major Expenses
key_items: 1.15 Disclosure required as per Ministry of Corporate Affairs notification dated 24 March, 2021
1.16 Expenses exceeding 1% of the total income
nodes.summary: The page presents two disclosure sections from financial statements. Section 1.15 addresses Ministry of Corporate Affairs notification compliance, stating that for years ended 31 March 2025 and 2024, the Bank and its subsidiaries did not grant advances, loans, investments, guarantees, or security with any understanding to further lend or invest for identified persons, nor did they receive funds with any understanding to further lend, invest, or provide guarantees on behalf of identified persons, excluding normal banking transactions. Section 1.16 lists other expenditure items exceeding 1% of total group income for 2025 (DSA commissions, network partner charges, cashback charges, PSL certificate purchase charges) and 2024 (DSA commissions, professional fees, cashback charges, business promotion expenses, network partner charges), with corresponding amounts in crores.

nodes.title: 1.17 Additional information pursuant to Schedule III of the Companies Act, 2013
nodes.summary: The text presents additional information pursuant to Schedule III of the Companies Act, 2013, for Axis Bank Limited and its group entities for the years ended March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024. It details net assets and profit or loss for the parent, subsidiaries, step-down subsidiaries, minority interest, and associate, both in absolute amounts (₹ in crores) and as a percentage of consolidated net assets and profit or loss. The data includes entities such as Axis Capital Limited, Axis Trustee Services Limited, Axis Mutual Fund Trustee Limited, Axis Asset Management Company Limited, Axis UK Limited, Axis Finance Limited, Axis Securities Limited, Freecharge entities, A.Treds Limited, Axis Pension Fund Management Limited, Axis Capital USA LLC, and Axis Max Life Insurance Company Limited. Footnotes clarify that amounts are before inter-company adjustments and that consolidated net assets are total assets minus total liabilities including minority interest.

nodes.title: 1.18 Description of contingent liabilities
nodes.summary: The text details the Group's contingent liabilities: (a) disputed claims from legal cases and tax/statutory demands, with a provision of ₹904.76 crores for probable claims; (b) unpaid liabilities for partly paid investments; (c) forward exchange contracts, including NDFs, where contingent liability is the notional principal, with offsetting inter-bank transactions reducing net market risk; (d) derivative contracts such as currency options/swaps, exchange-traded options, non-deliverable derivatives, interest rate/currency futures, FRAs, and currency futures, with contingent liability as notional principal and similar offsetting; (e) guarantees issued on behalf of constituents, net of cash margin; and (f) acceptances, endorsements, and other obligations like documentary credits and bills, also net of cash margin.

nodes.title: Contingent Liabilities from Derivatives, Guarantees, and Investments
key_items: d) Liability on account of derivative contracts
e) Guarantees given on behalf of constituents
nodes.summary: The page covers contingent liabilities: (b) unpaid amounts for partly paid investments; (c) forward exchange contracts including NDFs, with notional principal as contingent liability and offsetting inter-bank transactions reducing net risk; (d) derivative contracts—currency options/swaps, exchange-traded currency options, non-deliverable derivatives, interest rate/currency futures, FRAs—explaining each instrument and similar notional principal and offsetting treatment; and (e) guarantees issued on behalf of customers as irrevocable assurances, stated net of cash margin, in Schedule 12 Contingent Liabilities.

nodes.title: f) Acceptances, endorsements and other obligations
nodes.summary:
f) Acceptances, endorsements and other obligations
These include documentary credit issued by the Bank on behalf of its customers and bills drawn by the Bank’s customers that are accepted or endorsed by the Bank. These are stated net of cash margin held with the Bank as on the reporting date in Schedule 12 – Contingent Liabilities of the Balance Sheet.

nodes.title: g) Other items for which the Group is contingently liable
nodes.summary: The text covers contingent liabilities (bills rediscounted, capital contracts, forex contracts, investment purchases, indemnity, NPAs, IPO commitments, associate investment, DEAF), assessment of long-term contracts for foreseeable losses with adequate provisions. It includes prior-year figure reclassification, auditor signatures, directors' and company secretary's signatures. It presents Form AOC-1 with Part A subsidiaries' financial details (capital, reserves, assets, liabilities, income, profit, tax, dividend, shareholding), notes on currency conversion, dividend non-recognition, and no liquidated/commenced subsidiaries. Part B details the associate (Max Life Insurance) with balance sheet date, acquisition date, shares, investment, holding, net worth, profit. Part C is not applicable. Basel III disclosures are referenced via website link.
